text: Although specifically requested; fss briefer fails to provide relevant notams for heli pilot's IFR destination airport.
A320 flight crew reports landing gear failure to retract after takeoff and ecam message; landing gear shock absorber fault.
B747 Captain laments the continuing problem of ground equipment being parked inside the safety zone at the SFO International terminal.

B757 captain reports #1 engine quitting shortly after being started. Maintenance can find no faults. Crew flies two legs with no problems but engine quits again after start on third leg; the flight was subsequently cancelled.
Air carrier flight crew on departure from mdw experiences a speed deviation on the midway 7 SID. The captain cites speed restriction 'buried' in the notes section of the chart as contributory.
A320 flight crew reports bird strike at 500 ft on departure. Vibration is noted and the crew declares an emergency and returns to departure airport.
B767-300 captures false GS and descends below cleared altitude while cleared for the ILS to Runway 28 at ORD.
show: 2008-12 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Initial Approach

text: B737 departure from ONT described multiple altitude assignments; a TCAS TA; all allegedly because the ATC controller erred in separation efforts.
B757-200 suffered right engine failure. Flight crew declared emergency and diverted to nearest suitable airport.

A crj-200 pilot reports that an unknown person with sida identification placed two full oxygen bottles on the aircraft after being told the aircraft's destination was not the intended destination for the bottles.

A crj-900 pilot reported a bleed air leak in the anti-ice duct after departing in icing conditions disabling the anti-ice system. Following QRH procedures the crew continued to their cold IMC destination with no problem.

A B737-800 pilot reports an aggressive autopilot pitch down to a minus 5 degrees at 2200 ft on an ILS approach to sea 16L. One aircraft was in position on runway 16C and otherwise no ILS interference was noted.
show: 2008-12 · Inflight: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Initial Approach

text: A SR22 pilot departed from a towered airport without takeoff clearance because the atis message noting the tower closure was incorrect and his aircraft's radio volume was turned too low to hear pre-takeoff responses to CTAF and tracon after departing.
Two small aircraft have a nmac at cps; the local controller did not proactively tell both aircraft about each other for visual identification.
A B757 pilot rejected a takeoff at 100-110 kts after an eicas rev indication alerted.

An A320 crew reports that a FAA inspector noted a baggage and freight count different from that shown on the weight and balance. The crew requested a baggage shift and new in range weight and balance.

A B737-300 crew conducted a loc bc approach with a 500 ft ceiling and 3 mile visibility. At 400 ft the captain took the aircraft and both pilots shifted to outside monitoring allowing a high sink rate. A go-around was initiated.
B757 captain believes revised MEL allowing unconditional deferral of the wing illumination lights is unsafe because of the need to inspect for the presence of ice on wings at night.

A B717 pilot complains that flight attendants use an air freshener on the forward lav that may be hazmat. The chemical spray in the air conditioning system enters the flight station causing pilots physical discomfort.
During preflight a B737 crew turned the 'b' hydraulic pumps off and 'a' hydraulic pumps on due to wind conditions. During engine start the tow bar broke when the 'a' system pressurized.
An air carrier crew missed the okain altitude restriction on the san loc 27 approach programming the FMC transition from the baret 4 to the approach.
show: 2008-12 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Initial Approach

text: An A319 captain reports ATC consistently requires lower descent altitudes requiring more fuel. Dispatch did not account for the added fuel burn until called by the reporter.
An A320 crew failed to close the APU bleed valve prior to deicing and the aircraft cabin filled with smoke. The station de-ice procedure and fatigue were both issues.
show: 2008-12 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Parked
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: An SF340 executed a missed approach when the airport's snow plow did not exit the runway while on an ILS approach. The plow's radio malfunctioned.

EMB145 flight crew reports a Captain's pitot static system failure during descent in icing conditions. First Officer becomes flying pilot and lands safely. Post flight reveals ice in tube and failed pitot heat.
An air carrier captain reports injuring a flight attendant while stopping abruptly for a catering truck that did not yield as the aircraft entered the gate area.
CL604 Captain reports missing crossing restriction at REGLE on the JAIKE2 RNAV arrival to TEB after First Officer commands a leveloff at 9000 ft.
show: 2008-11 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Initial Approach

text: B737 flight crew rejects second takeoff; cargo door warning is MEL'ed; but crew fails to read MEL book and understand that warning is to be ignored.
B737 flight crew fails to note 250K speed restriction on the midway 7 SID.
Student pilot on solo cross country gets confused departing psp and takes off without clearance from the tower.
MD82 flight crew reports an engine failure on short final and after emergency declaration; a normal landing ensues.
MEM Controller experienced operational error when assuming an altitude assignment had been accomplished; but in fact had not; resulting in the conflict.
B737 flight crew is cleared to cross Runway 24L and cleared for takeoff on Runway 24R. Crew turns on Taxiway C and attempts takeoff before being informed of error by Tower Controller.
A B737 flight crew noticed abnormally low airflow from the lavatory vent. They wrote up the discrepancy and were disappointed when the maintenance resolution was to accept the low flow as normal.
A320 flight crew experience a dual FMGC failure on initial climbout and return to their departure station for repairs.
A lead mechanic reports a B737-700 brake assembly was inadvertently installed on a B737-800 at the left outboard (#1) position of the left main landing gear.
PHL controller described an unauthorized takeoff when two same company aircraft with similar sounding four-digit flight numbers and readbacks became confused; one taking off without a clearance.
B777 captain questions current methods of checking pilot age to insure at least one pilot is under age 60 to comply with icao standards.
A319 brake temperature indicators show one brake hot upon gear extension for landing. After landing inspection determines it to have been an apparently false indication.
General aviation pilot practicing ILS approaches to vdf is distracted attempting to use cockpit automation and flies over lal at 1800 feet while sky divers are descending overhead and to the north.
show: 2008-12 · Airspace Violation All Types · Initial Approach

text: A pa-28 pilot was conducting steep turns about a point and entered class d airspace at less than 1000 ft. During the turns; a g-inducted fuel stream came off of the wing causing the pilot to declare an emergency and land at the airport.
A B757-200 flight crew noted a (right) rev indication on eicas during takeoff and elected to reject.
A320 captain believes acr company operations manual and a MEL procedure regarding cockpit door access keypads are not compatible.

B767 flight crew uses wrong altimeter setting descending through transition level (29.41 set with actual setting of 30.41) resulting in altimeter reading 1000 ft high. Egpws terrain warning is annunciated during visual ILS at 900 ft AGL with the aircraft on glide slope and on the PAPI. Go around is initiated and the altimeter error is discovered.
A320 captain reports fmgc automatically activated approach phase mode approaching queny on the eagul2 arrival to phx; causing the aircraft to slow unexpectedly.
B737 flight crew reports track deviation after runway change during the skees2 RNAV arrival to slc.
show: 2008-12 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Descent

text: An atr with a deferred fuel quantity system annunciated a fuel low level light after takeoff. The crew forgot this was a normal indication with the known fault and in error they returned to land.
show: 2008-12 · Procedural: Published Material / Policy · Initial Climb

text: CRJ200 flight crew receives incorrect pet weight from Load Planning. Corrected later in flight. No weight and balance limits exceeded.

An A300's #1 thrust reverser was MEL'ed and locked out prior to flight. After takeoff the green #1 reverser deployed light and associated ecam illuminated. An emergency was declared with a return to land.
Widebody captain reports speed restr note for departures to the s on the ORD3 spells the cmsky fix as cemsky on his commercial charts and leads to exceeding speed limit.
Crj-200 flight crew declare an emergency and returned to departure airport after experiencing a 'loud thump' accompanied by an airframe shudder shortly after takeoff.
Enroute Controller described loss of communications and radar contact with VFR general aviation aircraft; resulting in unplanned landing at alternate airport; aircraft experienced alternator failure.
General aviation pilot taxied into position at CID described controller spacing judgment error that resulted in a Regional Jet being issued go-around.
A B747-400 crew describes the events leading up to a foreign airport landing with all of the flight attendants standing after the pilot landing announcement five minutes prior.
B757-200 captain reports reactive windshear encounter on approach to bdl.
B737 flight crew fails to note the 250 kt speed restriction on the ORD3 SID.
B747-400 flight crew fails to make prepare for landing announcement. Some cabin attendants are standing upon landing.

During cockpit preflight; pilot notices the portable halon fire extinguisher discharge nozzle hose was not secured on an airbus A319. Fire bottle is mounted to the AFT bulkhead circuit breaker panel and loose hose could pop one of the breakers during turbulence.
General aviation pilot unable to execute ILS approach at fuel stop airport because of equipment problems was given ASR approach by ATC resulting in a safe landing.
PA28 pilot is questioned by approach control for flying the DME arc transition between JIBTO and DUPNT on the GPS Runway 18 approach to IMM.
show: 2008-12 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Initial Approach

text: Ga pilot reports penetrating tcm airspace at 2500 ft while attempting to land at plu. Fiddling with gps is cited as a contributing factor.
show: 2008-12 · Airspace Violation All Types · Initial Approach

text: CRJ900 flight crew experiences high ITT and associated EICAS warnings shortly after engine start. Reporter addresses ambiguity of response as a result of inconsistent training regarding dealing with engine start abnormalities.
B757-200 First Officer reports difficulty taxiing to de-icing area with snow obscuring side windows. Feels windows should have been cleaned prior to taxi.
B757 Captain returns to gate to repair inoperative wing inspection light due to inability to perform pre-departure check in snow storm.
An air carrier pilot reports excessive glide slope fluctuations at 700 ft while flying a coupled ILS to sea runway 16L.
show: 2008-12 · Procedural: Published Material / Policy · Initial Approach

text: ZBW controller described conflict event when visual separation descent clearance was rescinded but air carrier descended and separation was lost.

A319 flight crew reports being informed in flight that hazmat has been incorrectly loaded. After return and aircraft swap hazmat is again loaded incorrectly. Error is caught prior to takeoff this time.
A B737-300 flight crew was unable to select another frequency after takeoff on either VHF radio; so they returned to land at their departure airport.

An airbus flight crew experienced loss of oil pressure in cruise flight. They shut down the engine; declared an emergency; and diverted to the nearest suitable airport after consulting with dispatch and maintenance.
B737 flight crew receives low altitude alert from ATC during ILS 24 approach to ISP. Crew started descent prior to LOC capture.
show: 2008-12 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Initial Approach

text: A B737-700 flight crew experienced smoke in the cabin shortly after takeoff. They declared an emergency and returned to land at the departure airport.
show: 2008-12 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Takeoff
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: Unwilling to fly an aircraft with an inoperative APU; first officer of an A320 is advised he would face disciplinary action by his company for refusing to fly the aircraft into widespread bad weather.
A320 flight crew; reporting for early morning departure; discover aircraft has been deiced without configuring the aircraft In Accordance With company SOP.
Crj-900 returned to departure airport due to a lavatory smoke alarm.
show: 2008-12 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Initial Climb
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: Boi controller described event when aircraft cleared for loc bc 28L; instructed to maintain 8000 until established; descended to 6900 ft; questioning mva versus crossing restrictions.
show: 2008-12 · ATC Issue All Types · Initial Approach

text: Air Carrier landing ORD described ATC directed go around event because of runway incursion alert and subsequent questionable pattern vectors for a second approach.
show: 2008-12 · ATC Issue All Types · Initial Approach

text: Private pilot of PA28 diverts to nearby airport when weather deteriorates.
VFR general aviation aircraft departing SNS Runway 26 described NMAC when conflict occurred with departing southbound helicopter. Reporter claims both ATC and helicopter pilot erred causing event.
B737 first officer reports TCAS RA; altitude deviation and degraded performance on approach and landing. Discover loss of performance due to airframe icing on the horizontal and vertical stabilizers.
An md-80 flight crew lost pressurization; declared an emergency; descended to a lower altitude; and landed at their destination.
A DA42 pilot experienced left engine surging and later complete engine failure. The pilot was able to restart the engine on the ground without any indication of a malfunction.

Enroute VFR C172 at 4500 with TUS Approach Controller experienced NMAC when Controller's traffic call clock position and turn instructions were based upon the wrong location of the conflicting traffic.

During takeoff; home-built vans rv-9A pilot notices the subaru engine rpm's and the mt propeller rpm's had redlined. Pilot declared emergency shortly after smelling engine burning. Normal landing; no prop or engine damage.
An A300 flight crew experienced nose gear unsafe lights after extending landing gear. They followed the manual gear extension procedure and landed normally.
BE20 flight crew experiences fluctuating oil pressure and elects to shut down the engine and divert. A loose oil dipstick permitted oil loss.
Very Light Jet (VLJ) departure from PDK described conflict at 1;500 FT with unreported helicopter on the Tower frequency; reporter alleging Local Controller was remiss in not issuing traffic.

After performing a fuel summation unit (fsu) change and adjustment; two mechanics were informed that the flight crew had reported the B737-300 had experienced an incorrect fuel load and a corresponding lateral imbalance.
A P180 captain and first officer ehsi's and eadi's became unusable in flight after having departed in rain showers. Maintenance discovered moisture in the radome avionics bay.
After a paperwork audit; two mechanics are informed the nose tires they installed on a B737-700 were the wrong effectivity.
Mechanic reports on the misunderstanding and releasing of a B737-300 with forward galley carts missing.

Confrontational cabin attendants during debrief of a landing during which an unseated attendant received minor injuries causes B747 captain to question whether the chain of onboard command has been institutionally degraded.
B737 captain reports unsatisfactory deicing experience at hou.
Captain reports track deviation on the haray3 RNAV departing clt. Transition is not reentered after runway change just prior to departure as required by this FMC.
show: 2008-12 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Climb

text: Mechanic notices the calibration due date of their HF coupler test equipment had expired. Three of their B737-300 HF antenna couplers had to be recalled and retested; because they were calibrated after the test equipment due date.
A319 responds to TCAS RA while flying parallel approach to Runway 27L at ORD.
Air carrier first officer notices the shifty RNAV arrival into rsw conflicts with a current NOTAM.

A B717 rejected its takeoff at 80 kts after a computer fault indicating a stabilizer problem caused a master caution light; EAD annunciation; and an aural warning. All indications and settings were normal prior to takeoff throttle up.
A pilot flying the same B747-400 on different occasions; notices the numerous times write-ups on the #3 utility/galley electrical busses and equipment; have been signed off by maintenance as okay.
A B757 Captain successfully rejected a takeoff after V1 when his ADI and HSI lost data input. The aircraft's weight was light and the runway was long.

A DHC8-400 Captain allowed passenger boarding on an extremely cold day as the APU warmed the aircraft. Late in the de-ice procedure the APU bleeds were reopened to allow heating. Subsequently the aircraft filled with smoke and was evacuated.
A B747-400's nose landing gear did not retract after takeoff. The crew returned to land after dumping fuel in holding.

A CRJ-700 taxied onto a ramp with NIL braking and used maximum reverse to stop the aircraft from colliding with another aircraft. Airport authorities treated the ramp before the aircraft could taxi to the gate.
show: 2008-12 · Ground: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Taxi

text: An ERJ-190 'Flaps Fail' EICAS message alerted as the flaps were extended on approach. An emergency was declared followed by a slats full; flaps 5 landing.
An A319's reversers did not open on landing because the hydraulic shutoff valves controlling them were left closed following an extended hanger maintenance cycle.
A B757 'Left Engine Fuel Filter' EICAS alerted after takeoff. The aircraft returned to land while ATC declared an emergency for the flight.

Pilot reported when he was on approach; he disconnected the B767-300 autopilot and noticed the roll control of aircraft was abnormal. When moving the yoke to roll aircraft to regain loc centerline; the yoke became difficult to move to increase roll rate.
Lear31 captain reports pitot static system failure during descent resulting in descent below assigned altitude. The crew declared an emergency; and an uneventful approach and landing ensued.
MD90 Captain reports compressor stalls upon leveloff at FL240. Engine thrust is retarded to idle and flight returns to departure airport after declaring an emergency.
Mechanic realizes after a B767-300 had departed; that he replaced the left transponder with a transponder having a different number. Mechanic had transposed numbers; causing the error.
After landing; an antique fighter lost hydraulic pressure causing a brake failure. Aircraft steering is with brakes so subsequently with no steering the aircraft exited the taxiway.

Beechcraft Premier One flight crew is directed to go-around on final approach due to the preceding aircraft's failure to clear the runway in a timely fashion. They enter overlying Class C Airspace while doing so.

An air carrier pilot reports a spatial disorientation on a night downwind arrival for ABQ Runway 26 that caused the crew to approach Runway 30 in a strong crosswind. A go-around was executed followed by an approach to Runway 26.

After releasing a B737-500 with a continuing MEL for a chronic cabin pressurization 'auto fail' light; mechanic was informed he should have grounded the aircraft and performed a pressurization health check prior to departure.

While on an autopilot coupled approach to SEA Runway 16L at 10 DME; the aircraft pitched up 5 degrees then down 6 degrees and accelerated to 170 kts exceeding the flap 30 speed for 2 seconds. An aircraft was taxiing across in front of Runway 16L and another was on short final.

a DHC8-400 'Flap Power' caution alerted during descent. After resetting the fault; the 'Flap Drive' caution alerted. An emergency was declared and a no-flap landing followed. The 'Flap Power' anomaly occurred on the previous flight also.

An EMB145 flight crew reports capturing a false glideslope during an ILS 28 approach to ORD. Glideslope indications were normal. ATC alerted the crew to an altitude deviation. After stopping the descent the ILS glideslope low indication appeared.
show: 2008-12 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Initial Approach

text: An EMB140 engine Low Pressure Vibration rose rapidly to maximum during climb after takeoff. The flight attendant smelled burning oil. The engine was shut down; an emergency was declared and the aircraft returned to land.

An A320 crew reported at an overnight station the aircraft water and systems froze the previous night. While preparing the aircraft for flight; a delay resulted that was falsely blamed on the crew because the station personnel did not keep the aircraft warm.
B777 flight crew reports engine overheat and bleed air anomalies during climb at 13000 feet and after declaring an emergency; return for an uneventful overweight landing.

An air carrier pilot executed a go-around on an ILS to DEN 35L after receiving a TCAS RA climb command while conducting a parallel approach. In the climb ice was accumulated leading to a stick shaker and loss of altitude.
show: 2008-12 · Inflight: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Landing

text: B737ng suffers apparent fuel leak in right engine fuel system. Shut down engine and divert per QRH checklists.
B777 ferry flight returns to departure airport after experiencing an apparently false fire warning in the crew rest area during the climb.
show: 2008-12 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Climb
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: DA10 flight crew on CSHEL ONE RNAV SID out of RSW levels at 530 ft vice 4000 ft MSL based on misreading of Government aero chart symbology.
Air carrier flight crew misses their right turn on taxiway 'c' at tjsj; citing lack of adequate signage as a contributing factor.
CLT Controller working adjacent sector observed what was believed to be a loss of separation with departures from parallel Runways 18L/18R.
Dhc8-400 flight attendant is unable to open the rear aircraft doors after an emer landing; they are frozen shut.
SF340 flight crew suffers hydraulic system anomalies immediately after takeoff. Returned to departure airport under emergency conditions and performed zero flap landing.
B757 flight crew must declare fuel emergency at ZZZ account unplanned delays due to airport configuration change.
ERJ on the O'Hare Three SID from ORD fails to comply with the 250 kt restriction sequestered in the fine print at the top of the page.
Widebody flight crew experience transitory stick shaker when maneuvering at minimum clean airspeed assigned by ATC.
Flight crew of heavy transport aircraft fail to follow back course of localizer as cleared following takeoff from Runway 16R at RNO which wasn't correct either for their departure runway.
Cessna 210 pilot suffers catastrophic engine failure shortly after takeoff. Lands safely in field.
MD80 diverts to the nearest suitable airport following an engine start valve open anomaly.

During a reposition taxi of a B757-200; two mechanics were alerted by a chime and noticed the right engine oil pressure dropping and an egt exceedance over 900 degrees centigrade; requiring the #2 engine to be shut down.
A corporate pilot notes that RNAV arrivals are routinely assigned and then modified so that there is confusion over whether it is a 'via' clearance or not.
show: 2008-12 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Descent

text: A B737-800 crew diverts to a nearby airport when both engine drive hydraulic pumps indicate low pressure.
PA31 pilot reports running out of oxygen at 17000 ft and diverting to nearest suitable airport.

DHC-8 flight crew observes 'select' light illuminated after engine start and applies wrong QRH procedure prior to departing. Enroute the crew is informed by maintenance that starter failure is indicated and they should not have departed.
C172 pilot reports oil pressure dropping and eventual engine failure. Reporter makes safe landing in farmers field without damaging aircraft.
A mechanic is informed he improperly placarded and deferred a B757-200 wheel well fire warning system after the aircraft required an air turnback for a wheel well fire indication.

A line avionics mechanic is informed the B757-200 write up he signed off for a leading edge slat disagree light and eicas warning when flap positions selected; had reoccurred at the next arrival station.

Three mechanics report on their involvement and trouble shooting of an airbus A320 that was found with an incomplete reassembly of the nose gear upper torque link; causing faults on numerous flights; an air turnback and a ferry flight for maintenance repairs.
As the weather deteriorates below that forecast; a helicopter pilot decides to divert to a nearby airport.

Mechanic reports an B757-200 made an air turnback after reinstalling the left engine inlet nose cowl following an attrition liner repair. The p-1 sense line for the EPR transmitter and fuel flow governor was found loose.
PA46 pilot reports a runway excursion after a normal touchdown on a dry runway with calm wind.
C182 pilot reports a runway excursion during a crosswind landing; causing minor damage to aircraft.

A mechanic reports being intimidated by a lead mechanic and given discipline by the manager while trying to verify that an airworthiness directive (ad) had been accomplished on two fuel boost pumps prior to installing them on a B757-200.
ATR72 flight crew reports go-around due gusty crosswind conditions and does not hear Tower assigned missed approach altitude; which they exceed.
ZJX controller described loss of separation at approximately 12;000 FT; when air carrier failed to comply with altitude restriction; conflicting with another aircraft.
show: 2008-12 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Initial Approach

text: Lear Captain reports low altitude alert from TEB Tower during LOC 19 approach and exceeding missed approach altitude during the missed.
SR22 pilot reports altitude deviation with autopilot on and altitude select at 9000 feet on the PFD. Loss of communication between PFD and autopilot is suspected.
show: 2008-12 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Cruise

text: B757 flight attendant discovers enroute that two Federal Air Marshals are on board that have not been identified to the flight crew.
ZBW controller described operational deviation when limited data block was not noted by relieving controller and aircraft entered adjacent airspace without a handoff.
Cabin attendant aboard undisclosed air carrier aircraft reports gear failed to retract and an emergency was declared. Flight returned to departure airport after burning fuel for about one hour.
Dash 8 flight crew reports deicing boom making contact with horizontal stabilizer during deicing operation. Crew returns to gate.
A319 suffers two flat tires on the nose gear following a normal landing.

An A320's right wing inspection/scan light was inoperative during night and snow operations. The MEL prohibits release under these conditions; yet until the flight crew refused the aircraft; Maintenance was not inclined to repair the light.
A B737-300 Captain reported losing some systems after a DC Bus breaker popped. A reset was unsuccessful; and after checking weather they decided to continue to destination.
Flight crew of unspecified air carrier aircraft on an ILS PRM approach are instructed to go around by the Monitor Controller due to encroachment by the partner aircraft.
SF340 captain reports receiving inaccurate field condition reports for destination airport.
CRJ200 experiences failure of the nose gear to retract after takeoff. Return to departure airport.
A B757-200 Captain reported deviating from the LGA Whitestone Climb when his inexperienced First Officer got behind the aircraft.
Flight crew of heavy transport aircraft fail to follow back course of localizer as cleared following takeoff from Runway 16R at RNO.
MD11 flight crew reports ATC directed go around that results in an altitude deviation and a declaration of emergency fuel. Aircraft lands with 5500 LBS of fuel on board.
GV flight crew discovers that they are not familiar with QNH procedures while being vectored for approach at UUWW. Crew gets 700 feet low when instructed to descend to 600 meters.
Nose gear of Cessna 337 fails to retract after takeoff and cannot be extended fully for landing. Collapses during roll out and aircraft exits the runway.
A C150 pilot experienced engine failure and executed a forced landing in a field.

A mechanic reports a B767-300 arrived with a log item the hp valve will not stay open at low power settings or on descent. He performed the MEL procedure; but he inadvertently locked out the wrong valve on #2 engine causing an air turnback.

First Officer of C-9b (military DC-9-30) reacts inappropriately to false GPWS Terrain Warning while in cruise at FL340. Reporter cites fatigue and diurnal desynchronosis for the loss of situational awareness.
show: 2008-12 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Cruise

text: L30 controller described conflict event when departure; assigned NOTWN2; initially turned the wrong direction; was corrected by ATC; assigned several intermediate altitudes; but eventually resulted in questionable separation.
Transatlantic B767-300 diverts to first available suitable airport due burning smell from air conditioning system vents.
show: 2008-10 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Cruise
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: A mechanic reports on installing a B737-800 APU battery in a B757-200 aircraft. Both batteries look identical and are functionally equivalent to each other; but the part numbers are not.
CRJ200 First Officer receives a low altitude alert from TLH Tower during GPS 18 approach. Incorrect minimums of 520 ft are being used when aircraft capabilities require minimums of 800 ft.
VFR twin engine turboprop pilot with PCT described potential conflict at 13;500 with IFR air carrier; ATC directed turn away from traffic.
Air carrier captain described minimum fuel event when ATC elected to declare emergency for the pilot.
show: 2008-12 · ATC Issue All Types · Initial Approach

text: B737 flight crew reports accepting checked luggage in the passenger cabin due to weight and balance considerations.
Maintenance defers an operational engine fire detector vice the associated bottle squib on a B737NG. Mistake undetected by flight crew prior to subsequent departure.
CRJ-200 flight crew requires deicing prior to departure then experiences toilet smoke EICAS one minute after takeoff. Glycol smoke is suspected and crew returns for uneventful landing.
Dash8-100 flight crew reports being dispatched with KNS navigation system MEL'ed and discovers; once airborne; that the VOR receiver is also inoperative. Crew elects to return.
B717 Captain reports slat disagree warning during approach although slats have extended normally. A normal full flap and slat landing ensues using manual thrust selection.
B737 Captain reports difficulties with aircraft automation while attempting to intercept the LOC Runway 27 at SAN.
show: 2008-12 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Initial Approach

text: B757 Captain reports being assigned an aircraft for a part 91 ferry flight with passengers aboard. The aircraft also had a required piece of equipment on MEL.
B737 Captain encounters jet blast in the flare from a B747 holding between the parallel runways.
A320 flight crew abandoned approach when they encountered severe turbulence. Diverted and declared fuel emergency due to low fuel state.
show: 2009-02 · Inflight: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Initial Approach

text: After installing a cockpit APU start panel on a B757-200; a mechanic is later informed by his manager; the start panel was not effective for that aircraft.
Citation check captain reports exceeding both altitude and airspeed limitations on the dalton departure from teb. Lack of recent experience is cited as the primary cause.
A CRJ200 flight crew experienced extreme airframe vibration after takeoff. They declared an emergency and returned to land.
A C650 departed the runway after landing when the nose wheel steering made a hard right turn after landing without pilot input or ability of pilot to control travel.
DA40 rear door is opened during flight by toddler passenger.
CRJ200 must declare a fuel emergency and land enroute. Appear to have taken off without planned fuel on board.
On approach a CRJ700 flight crew received a gear disagree EICAS message. Unable to resolve the issue; they declare an emergency with ATC and upon landing the left gear collapses.
IFR general aviation aircraft departure from DRO; utilizing ODP procedures; ask ATC routing question/s; resulting in confusion regarding appropriate altitude assignments.
Citation captain reports exceeding 1500 ft prior to the teb 4.5 DME on the TEB5 departure. Misinterpretation of the procedure is cited as cause.
CL65 flight crew on a ferry flight experiences uncontrollable runway excursion. Subsequent to the event they notice the right thrust reverser failed to stow; the aircraft did not incur any damage.
A crj-200 pilot reports light to moderate wake vortex including a stall warning and stick shaker for 1 second at 1000 ft after takeoff behind an A320 aircraft.
show: 2008-12 · Inflight: Wake Vortex Encounter · Initial Climb

text: PA28 pilot on IFR flight plan reports encountering icing conditions and descending below MVA to get clear.

A helicopter manufacturer will be manufacturing and testing its medium and heavy helicopters at a facility located off the mqs airport near the approach end of runway 11. Operations will be a potential conflict for arriving and departing mqs VFR traffic.

Two aircraft inspectors describe the confusion and complexity of performing Receiving Inspection documentation on a Horizontal Stabilizer Trim Actuator (HSTA) for their CRJ-700 from an outside vendor; that also involved a secondary vendor.
C172 pilot departing CDW experiences an NMAC with a helicopter on the MMU LOC.
ZOB Controller experienced operational error at approximately FL350 when failing to note conflicting traffic prior to issuing descent clearance to another aircraft.
Cessna pilot reports landing on closed runway at ort due to lack of knowledge of NOTAM closing runway. Aircraft is immediately stuck in snow.

CRJ200 flight crew reports discovering at FL260 that insufficient fuel has been boarded to complete their flight. With 1200 LBS of fuel at top of descent an emergency landing is made at the nearest suitable airport.
EMB170 flight crew reports failure of landing gear to retract properly after takeoff. Crew declares emergency and normal landing ensues after burning down to landing weight.

EMB190 First Officer reported inadvertent parking brake release by a Flight Attendant while being deiced. Aircraft rolled ahead but no damage occurred. The Captain was on a lavatory break requiring the Flight Attendant's presence.
Light aircraft pilot reports flying through R3005C at 8500 ft to discover after the fact that the area is hot above this altitude. Notam check prior to departure did not indicate this to be the case.
Light twin pilot described altitude assignment confusion with MKG controller during RNAV runway 26 approach to BIV; controller questioning descent from 4000 ft.

A320 flight crew reports calling in fatigued after diverting for windshear and turbulence; then declaring an emergency for minimum fuel. Flight is delayed 2.5 hours at the divert airport before continuing on at which point the call is made.
At bis a medium large transport jet pilot taxied onto narrow taxiway abeam C4 because the commercial airport chart indicated a taxiway with dimensions similar to c.

During numerous c-checks; mechanic notices the AFT fairing for flap tracks #1; #2; and #7; #8 on B757-200 aircraft; have arrived with their lube bushing tubes (sleeves) installed backwards. As a result; the tubes are not getting properly lubed.
B757 flight crew encounters severe turbulence east bound at FL370. No injuries occur; however crew elects to divert for maintenance inspection.
EMB145 First Officer reported bleed leak EICAS message shortly after takeoff. Flight Attendant confirmed smoke; emergency declared; engine shut down; and passengers are evacuated after landing.

CRJ900 Captain reports RIGHT BLEED LEAK at FL350 and eventual loss of pressurization due to automatic closing of the Pressure Regulating Shutoff Valve's. Crew is able to continue to destination at 10;000 FT; unpressurized.

text: B737 reserve Captain reports an extremely fatiguing month; with weather delays; diversions; and rescheduled trips. This results in a fatigue call to crew scheduling after a less than minimum rest over night.
With the passengers trapped on board due to a jetway frozen to the ground; fuelers begin fueling the aircraft with all exits disarmed; in violation of fueling requirements.
CRJ900 flight crew receives apparently false brake temperature warning upon beginning descent from FL330.
B737 Captain relates unacceptable de-icing procedures at BDL.
Abetted by the use of night vision goggles; helicopter pilot flies into IMC and; after encountering ice buildup; makes a slow descent to VMC and lands safely in a field.
After the left overwing slide was replaced; a mechanic reports the right overwing slide on a B767-300 deployed during the rearming procedure.
After pulling the aircraft of the hangar with his automobile due to ice and snow covered ramps; the pilot of an SR22 fails to remove towbar from the aircraft prior to takeoff.

A CL30 departed after being deiced and had smoke in the cockpit concurrent with an electrical fault cas annunciation. An emergency was declared with a return to land. Maintenance determined the smoke was de-ice fluid and the cas alert was false.

Upon receipt of a 'Bleed Air' trip EICAS warning; B737NG returns to the departure airport because of icing conditions at the destination. An emergency per company procedures for overweight landing.
ANC local controller described an on going event that involves approach controller's requesting higher than published runway light settings to achieve a higher RVR value.
show: 2008-12 · Procedural: Published Material / Policy · Final Approach

Failed engine bleed and associated pack on overland portion of ETOPS flight results in a diversion and overweight landing for B767-300ER.
Pilot of C182 lands to investigate low oil pressure indication. Finds no obvious reason and takes off only to have engine fail catastrophically.
Deadheading crew member reported ice shedding on the wing upper surface of B737NG during climb out.
Air carrier inbound to Runway 12R at SAT; was issued 2000 FT by ATC; received a GPWS alert and executed a go-around; a confirmed ATC altitude assignment error.

text: A B737 crew received an EGPWS Obstacle warning at 2500 FT near the OMA Runway 14L BUFFT FAF while descending to 2400 FT. A go-around was initiated but quickly abandoned and the glideslope recaptured for a normal approach.
A B737 crew received an EGPWS Obstacle warning near the OMA Runway 14L BUFFT FAF descending to 2400 ft at 600 fpm. A go around was completed followed by an uneventful approach.
ERJ Captain discusses a breakdown in CRM and command responsibility during an unstabilized approach flown by the First Officer.
B737-400 flight and cabin crews suffer carbon monoxide overexposure due to ground equipment exhausting into cabin prior to departure.
B737-300 flight crew encounters apparent ice build-up and eventual shedding somewhere in the rotating sections of the left engine.
DHC-8 gets stuck in a snow bank on the ramp. Blowing snow and poor braking action contributed to the event.
show: 2008-12 · Ground: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Taxi

text: Acr flight crew report exceeding the speed limit departing over cmsky on the mdway7 departure. Note is small and was overlooked in rushed preflt.

A Lead Mechanic signs off the replacement of a cabin halon fire extinguisher by a Repairman; because due date was unreadable. Replacement halon bottle was not effective for the B737-800; resulting in a configuration deviation release.
Pilot of Lancair on an IFR flight plan allows a non-current pilot to fly. A departure from cleared altitude and a loss of separation with other IFR traffic results.

text: A Mechanic; Lead Mechanic; Captain and First Officer report on the separation of the #1 engine core cowls on a B757-200 shortly after takeoff; with damage to the left wing flaps and horizontal stabilizer.
Cabin attendant reports inadequate cleaning of bodily fluids left on board by a passenger from the previous flight.
Destined for ZZZZ; transatlantic B777 diverts to ZZZZ1 account low fuel due to reroute and terminal delays. Must declare fuel emergency to obtain expedited handling for landing.
Loud noise following gear retractions leads EMB-140 flight crew to suspect the nose gear doors failed to close. Declare emergency and divert to another airport for maintenance.

E140 flight crew experience loud bang in the nose shortly after takeoff. Suspect nose gear anomaly and land under emergency conditions at destination. Reporter notes a flight two days earlier encountered a landing gear retraction anomaly for which Maintenance was unable to find a cause.

B777 flight crew returns to departure airport due to acrid odors emanating from the Air Conditioning System. Experience rudder anomalies associated with speed brake extension and retraction during descent.

A320 Captain reports failure of Maintenance to diagnose and repair log book write-ups. Feels the problem is systemic in the maintenance structure.
A B757-200 flight crew experienced an autopilot pitch over in descent that resulted in an altitude deviation.

RJ flight crew is dispatched to FAR with no alternate and none required according to the weather packet received from Dispatch. Enroute this is discovered to be in error. Actual forecast at time of departure required an alternate.
B737 flight crew reported track and altitude deviations during SADDE6 arrival to LAX. Arrival is compounded by equipment malfunctions; 100 knot tailwinds; and a misheard heading assignment.

A319 flight crew reports missing crossing restriction at REVUE on the ELDEE4 arrival to DCA. Restriction dropped from FMGC for unknown reasons.

text: A B757 was deiced with three days of ice and snow on the aircraft. During taxi the EQUIP COOLING EICAS alerted along with a popped circuit breaker and an electrical smell. An emergency was declared with a return for a gate evacuation.

Approach Controller advises Beechcraft 35 pilots they began descent for an approach fix without clearance. Pilots believe the clearance was given and forgotten by the Controller. Cite language barrier.
show: 2008-12 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Initial Approach

text: A CRJ-200 crew reports the effect of a Captain flying sick; fatigued and losing situational awareness while flying in adverse weather conditions.
An MD88 flight crew exceeded the 250 KT speed limit on departure out of ORD.
An MD80 flight crew slowed below assigned airspeed on final approach because they felt it was safer to do so given the turbulence and wind conditions.
A B737-300 flight crew failed to make a descent crossing restriction and the First Officer cited the consistently poor vertical navigation performance of the FMS.
show: 2008-12 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Descent

text: An A320 flight crew taxied onto a runway without clearance in part because the airport surfaces were snow covered.
After replacing the right engine CSD on an MD-80; a mechanic is later informed the same problem with the CSD (IDG) oil light flickering in flight; had reoccurred.
ZID handoff controller; providing OJT; failed to note an incorrect altitude issued by the RADAR controller.
show: 2008-12 · Procedural: Published Material / Policy · Initial Approach

text: A Maintenance Controller describes why he continued an MEL deferral of a B737-500 with a chronic cabin 'auto pressurization system' problem.

A mechanic qualified to taxi his carrier's MD-80's; but not qualified on the airport he is at on a field trip; has to rely on a contract maintenance person to work the radios. He was so fatigued; he does not remember receiving clearances all the way to the concourse.

A Repairman performing a composite repair of an A320 flap requiring continued moisture removal; reports on the unprofessional behavior of his maintenance supervisor; directing them to ignore the repair manual and 'just go fix it.'
An apparent false glide slope on an ILS approach to ORF caused a Lear 35 to descend below the actual GS.
Airline Dispatch failed to provide administrative support for flight crew of B777-200 who diverted to their alternate due to insufficient fuel to hold at their destination.

L2K landing at DVT described wrong runway landing event; 7R vs. 7L; claiming high performance aircraft; language issues on the frequency; last minute ATC change of runway and controller performance as contributory.

A Maintenance Controller realizes later he should have asked the pilot of a B737-300 with a right main gear indication showing both red and green lights; to make a write-up; instead of just asking him to cycle the gear.
Pilot and CFI aboard C172 fail to utilize appropriate CTAF procedures due to mismanagement of their radio volumes. Uncontrolled traffic pattern separation issue results.
A widebody transport aircraft enroute at FL260 with TBPB ATC experienced a TCAS RA with unreported large transport aircraft traffic.
A LR60 crew misaligned the HSI's after a battery start. No gyro vectors were required after takeoff before they finally aligned the systems for proper indications.
show: 2008-12 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Climb

text: A Dispatcher's responsibility for a medium transport jet was removed after the Dispatch Coordinator claimed that the flight's release was issued when the weather was below minimums. The flight was airborne but was recalled.
B747-400 Captain reports company fails to provide up-to-date field conditions for required 'suitable' airports available on polar route flights.

A flight crew taxiing at den is told to taxi to runway 17L via taxiways m; ed; and cn then hold short of runway 17R. Confusion results because no hold short lines exist on ed for runway 17R and the crew assumes cn ends at left and so is not entered during this taxi event.
SF340 on approach experiences multiple electrical failures. The crew requests vectors to run appropriate checklists; only for the problems to resolve themselves.

After start a SF340's engine flamed out as an engine condition lever was moved from the START position into the MIN-MAX range. The engine failure checklist was completed and the aircraft returned to the gate.
An A319 pilot reports ground deice crews are not waiting for flight crews to properly configure an aircraft before beginning deice fluid application as per the SOP.
A B737 crew reports that a Regional Jet taxiing at a high speed with its landing lights off in freezing rain failed to slow or yield to them and so nearly collided on ORD taxiway 'R.'
SF340 Captain reports communications breakdown with ATC during approach causing altitude deviations both leaving assigned altitude and attempting to return to it.
An A320 Captain wrote up his PFD enroute as being too dim even at maximum brightness; but at the next stop the outbound Captain said it was normal; and maintenance cleared the item.
A B757-200 flight crew experienced loss of left hydraulic system fluid and pressure. They declared an emergency; ran the QRH; and landed without incident.
An air carrier Captain reported concern with the company's scheduling practices and resulted fatigue.
Mechanic reports removing a leading edge bulb seal that was damaged during a pre-departure deicing on a DHC-8-Q400.
Air carrier Captain reports taxiway excursion from icy taxiway during taxi to the gate after landing.

In bound to ATL; CARJ-700 cleared to intercept the Rwy 9R ILS from the south with a 60 KT southerly wind was unable to capture the localizer. Approach quickly became unstabilized. Directed by ATC to go around. Subsequent approach was successful.
B777 Flight Attendant reports feeling dizzy during last portion of flight and the inability to remember passwords and telephone numbers after landing.
B757 landing DEN with D01 experienced TCAS RA with unreported VFR traffic; ATC indicating traffic was above Class B and observed after the event.
Air carrier landing RIC experienced TCAS RA descending from 14;000 FT with unreported traffic.

A B737-800 Captain and First Officer report the left engine overheat light illuminated at approximately 60 knots on two separate takeoff rolls; requiring rejected takeoffs. Maintenance found bleed duct disconnected and 12-14 insulators for the overheat detection circuit melted.

While enroute at FL360; pilot of a Challenger CL-604 noticed the #2 Air Data Computer (ADC) had failed; resulting in erroneous altitude indications and fluctuating airspeeds on both Primary Flight Displays.

B767 Captain reports being dispatched with an inoperative engine driven generator; with the APU providing the necessary second generator. Enroute the APU experiences auto shutdown several times and crew elects to divert.
Air carrier flight crew reports taxiway excursion during turn into the ramp; due to icy conditions and strong cross wind.

A11 Controller described a near loss of separation when a fellow controller requested aircraft be transferred to his/her sector on opposite base track; at the same altitude; resulting in a vector through the LOC to secure separation.
A CE560 flight crew overshot charted altitude by 300 ft on the teb 5 departure. The captain cited distraction following a joke by the tower controller as contributing.
B737 Captain reports lightning strike on downwind after go around. Aircraft was dispatched with radar deferred. Emergency is declared and remainder of approach is uneventful.
A GA pilot departed a California CTAF airport and discovered radio problems airborne. Possible violations of Class D and class C airspace occur prior to communications being reestablished.
Private pilot reports diversion to nearest suitable airport when enroute weather deteriorates. Reporter uses GPS to locate airport and to avoid terrain and obstacles at low altitude below clouds.
Mechanic reports the nose gear left axle spacer was found missing approximately nine months after he had replaced the left nose tire on a B777.
After replacing the right engine CSD on an MD-80; a Mechanic is later informed a loose 'B' nut was found at the CSD oil cooler on the Pratt Whitney JT-8 engine.
A contract maintenance Mechanic is informed he did not install the inboard axle spacers on the left and right nose tires on a B767-300.

A Mechanic; working as an Inspector; is informed a nose gear left axle washer was found missing; approximately six months after he had verified the left nose tire tang washer was installed on a B777-200.

B757-200 flight crew encounters leading and trailing edge flap anomalies on final approach. Minimum fuel situation complicates completing complex QRH procedures in a timely fashion. Land with flaps 1 degree.
A medium transport jet landed at JHW with NIL braking action after weather and NOTAM reports indicated light snow and only patchy snow and ice.

During a maintenance check on a B767-200; inspection found Rudder Ratio Changer Actuator hydraulic hose straps broken in the vertical stabilizer. Mechanic verified straps were not the modified types that records show as previously installed.
Approximately one week after replacing a NH speed sensor on a PW150A for the #1 engine on a DHC-8-400; Mechanic is informed the same speed sensor was found leaking oil.
A medium large aircraft could not taxi off of runway because of ice on the runway. Sand was applied and a tow vehicle pulled the aircraft to the gate.

An EMB145 dispatched with the automatic pressurization controller MEL'ed; was unable to control the cabin in manual mode. An emergency was declared but because of oxygen mask communications; ATC did not clearly understand as the aircraft descended to 10;000 FT.

A strong electrical smell developed in the aft galley of a B767-300 in cruise at FL370. Turning the utility bus switches off apparently solved the problem. An emergency was declared prior to landing because of an unusual noise in the galley.

A B717 First Officer experienced difficulty flying a raw data ILS approach when the autopilot disconnected following an unstabilized glideslope signal.

Mechanic reports three of the six maintenance check job cards that require deactivation of the leading edge slats and flaps on their B777-200's; do not have a reactivation procedure for the same slats and flaps prior to dispatch.

A DHC8-100s #1 starter/generator; GCU and bus tie all failed causing a variety of failures to the Captain's instruments; radios and NAVAIDS.

A DHC8-100s air-conditioning pack seized in flight causing smoke in the cabin. An emergency was declared with a diversion to a nearby airport where the passengers were deplaned on a taxiway. The smoke's cause was determined after the fact.

A CRJ-900's 'steering inop' EICAS alerted after takeoff. The pilot handbook procedure was followed and the flight continued to its destination. After landing the appropriate circuit breakers were reset allowing the aircraft to be taxied to its gate.
Following a complete electrical failure; pilot of a Cessna 177 utilized a cell phone to establish communications with HNL Tower and return for landing.

A pc-12 cas alerted 'unable FMS-gps mon;' 'gps 1 fail' and 'taws fail.' the pilot believed the indications were erroneous; but on a return ferry flight a map shift occurred along with failures of the autopilot; yaw dampener; and flight director.

A be-400 crew incorrectly set their altimeters to indicate 1000 ft high. While climbing on the teb 5 the aircraft was leveled at 1800 ft; really 800 ft; then a descent was begun to 1500 ft which would really be 500 ft.
Be35 pilot reports left traffic pattern for lhm runway 33 conflicts with newly instituted sky diver landing area on the west side of the airport.
A B737 crew reports a controller warned them because they did not follow a NOTAM and atis instruction arrivals on the rsw shfty one RNAV. The crew did not receive any modifications to the RNAV.

text: Maintenance incorrectly advised flight crew of A319 regarding position of MEL'ed outboard fuel transfer valves. Fuel transfers immediately upon takeoff.

An air carrier pilot cleared to taxi on mco c and j taxiways turned right on taxiway C1 because of a c taxiway sign abeam C1 indicating taxiway j was approaching.

An air carrier pilot landed at sfo following a cat iii approach and in the low visibility nearly taxied onto a closed and barricaded taxiway. The taxiway was closed after their previous departure but they were not notified of the NOTAM change enroute.

A B737-300 Trailing Edge (TE) Flap Disagree light alerted at 1000 ft on approach. After a go around; an emergency was declared followed by completion of the QRH procedure and a normal 15 degrees flap landing.

MDSD ATC; TRACON and Tower controllers were behind a bank of arriving aircraft and permitted an air carrier to cross the MDSD airport at 3000 FT. The aircraft's FMS database did not have an approach to a newly open runway complicating the approach.

One Hughes 500 main rotor blade was damaged by contact with the tail boom after gusty winds pushed the rotor down as it spun down on a parked helicopter. The crew landed to investigate an 'engine chips' light.
A BE76 instructor reports the aircraft's right flap outer track partially detached and in an upward bent position caused flight control problems. An emergency was declared followed by a safe landing.

Captain details incident where B757 First Officer reports for work ill; citing air carrier sick policies as an intimidating factor in his decision making.
B727-200 flight crew experiences an uncontrollable slide on the ramp while attempting to park.

ZOB controller experienced operational error at approximately FL320 during sequencing attempts for IAD; failing to note confliction in another area of the sector.

A mechanic assigned by his carrier to perform maintenance on a foreign carrier's B747-400; believed the deferral of a clogged mid cabin right galley H2O filter should have been under the logbook MEL and not the cabin log.

Prior to gate departure; B737 flight crew is advised of frost on top of wing surface by a concerned passenger.
Q400 flight crew experiences partial opening of baggage door at cruise. Declare emergency and divert to nearest suitable airport.

An ERJ170 flight crew got EICAS message FUEL FEED 2 FAULT and returned to departure airport. After turning back they got ENG 2 FUEL LOW PRESS. Reporter mentioned these items were written up the previous flight and cleared by maintenance.
B777 Captain reports interference; apparently from an AM commercial radio station; that hinders with ground crew/flight crew communications on pushback in SEA.
An ERJ170 flight crew got EICAS message FUEL FEED 2 FAULT and diverted to an enroute airport. After committing to divert they got ENG 2 FUEL LOW PRESS EICAS message.
A B757-200 flight crew experienced EICAS message GEAR UNSAFE on approach. They discontinued approach; declared an emergency; ran the procedure; and landed normally.
B757-200 nose gear fails to extend on final approach. Flight crew successfully performs alternate gear extension procedure and land safely following a precautionary emergency declaration.
Distracted by a Tower request to adjust the transponder; Captain of a Cessna 550 crosses the active runway without a clearance.
A C172 pilot experienced loss of power shortly after takeoff when he failed to check the magnetos during the runup.
Despite acceptable decelerometer reading on icy surfaces; B727-200 slides off ramp. Ultimately towed to gate.
B757 Captain reports engine failure passing 11;500 FT on climb out. Quick Reference Handbook procedures are complied with and flight returns for single engine landing.
E145 flight crew rejects takeoff due to blockage of the gust lock lever.
A g-iv departed on the teb 5. The captain was distracted by an amber windshear caution light and missed the 1500 ft level-off subsequently climbing to 1800 ft before descending.

MD88 Captain reports catastrophic engine failure climbing through 17000 feet with diversion to departure airport.

Mechanic reports about the confusion caused by the (SRM) Structural Repair Manual data that led to his not properly evaluating a dent on the right horizontal stabilizer leading edge of a B737-400.

text: A small transport pilot crossed the approach path to dhw runway 17L at taxiway e; citing faded hold short lines and a mis-communication problem.

A Chief Inspector of a repair station reports finding pictures of a small crack in the left forward transmission deck of a Eurocopter AS-350-B1. No log entry; no temporary repair; no damage limit criteria. The helicopter had been released for service and was flying.
A PA28 instructor pilot and his student experienced engine failure due to a defective fuel selector valve that failed to stop movement beyond the detent; shutting off the fuel supply.

A Lead Mechanic was informed he may have been involved in the installation of incorrect rivets that were installed as part of an Engineering Order for weight modification improvements on an EMB-145LR; two years earlier.
Nine months after installing a vendor overhauled nose landing gear on an A319; a Mechanic is notified both nose gear lock springs were found installed upside down.
An A319 flight crew experienced low fuel condition on arrival; declared an emergency; and landed normally.
CE680 Captain reports obstructions and chaotic conditions on the ramp at Ocean Reef airport; 07FA.
A11 controller described operational error event when departure was assigned routing that violated MVA standards.

B737 Captain reports difficulty stopping after landing on runway with braking action reported as 34/35/34. Reverse thrust is used to a complete stop as brakes are ineffective. Engine damage from FOD results.
A Captain and First Officer report an aborted takeoff due to aileron binding on their DHC-8-100.

EMB145 Captain reports noncompliance with MEL by fueler who refuses to over wing refuel and uses the MEL'ed pressure refueling system. Captain fails to inform Maintenance of this incident prior to departure.

On approach; a Saab-340B flight crew received a Terrain Awareness Warning System (TAWS) Terrain alert. During the following morning's first flight of the day checks; the TAWS test failed citing 'internal GPS not navigating.'
ATR72 First Officer reports engine failure shortly after departure at 10000 feet. Emergency is declared and flight returns to departure airport.

B737 flight crew is informed of track deviation after misinterpretation of PDC.

text: B737 flight crew reports cabin altitude fluctuations at FL370. Crew begins descent with oxygen masks on and regains control of pressurization by selecting alternate controller. Crew elects to divert and declare an emergency.
CRJ flight crew had to stop abruptly to avoid E145 taxiing across their runway at JFK.
A GIV Captain reported difficulty maintaining cabin pressure on a transpacific flight. He declared an emergency and returned to the mainland.
An LR55 flight crew noticed birds on takeoff roll and experienced failure of their landing gear to retract after takeoff.
An MD10 flight crew experienced a roll and an off course excursion when they deployed spoilers; apparently because of left wing spoiler failure.

P50 controller described operational error at 8500 when he/she issued unrestricted climb to a departure conflicting with arrival traffic.
A C182 pilot penetrated a skydiver jump area; where he had critical conflicts with skydivers and an experimental aircraft.
A B747-400 Captain reported confusion with a contractor fueling his aircraft; fuel imbalance limits were exceeded.
After an MD-80 departs the cabin fills with smoke. The flight crew declared an emergency and returned to land. Maintenance determined APU oil caused the smoke.
show: 2009-01 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Initial Climb

text: A B757 pilot reports inaccurate braking action reports from jac airport personnel. Actual braking action was fair when good was reported. Antiskid action caused a tire failure.
An air carrier pilot cleared to taxi from spot via m and n missed m and taxied over a non taxiway infield between n and m. The taxiway light locations confused the pilot.
An air carrier pilot departed on the CVG Bluegrass 8 but did not follow the SID routing because a NOTAM stated the procedure was not applicable for non-GPS equipped aircraft.
show: 2009-01 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Initial Climb

text: A B747-400 departing on a transatlantic international flight blew a tire on takeoff. After conferring with Dispatch and Maintenance about the nature of debris found on the runway they decided to dump fuel and return to their departure airport.
A light aircraft reported an NMAC with a helicopter at LDJ.

A LR35A nosewheel strut deflated after takeoff causing the nosewheel to retract turned thus preventing a safe nose gear up indication in flight. An emergency was declared followed by a normal landing at a diversion airport with Lear maintenance.
A CRJ-200's #2 engine failed at 6;000 FT on final. All QRH procedures were completed before an uneventful landing. The engine failure's cause was not determined.
Air carrier landing DFW questioned Controller's actions; i.e. aircraft crossing runway down field; reportedly when landing aircraft was still at 100 kts.
A B747 passenger became unruly attacking Cabin Attendants. The passenger was handcuffed and the flight diverted to an enroute oceanic destination.

A SF340's AC generator failed enroute. During landing the chip detect light illuminated. The generator was repaired but no chip defect was found. After takeoff; the chip detect light again illuminated. Upon returning to land a defective chip detector sending unit was found.

A large transport jet crew realized after landing that the their company's operations manual does not permit night landings on JAC Runway 01 because of high terrain. A GPWS warning was received during the approach.
A Captain reports he and his First Officer had just flown an A320 with aircraft batteries that had been out of date for several days. Their Maintenance Release was in error.

A CRJ700's CAS alerted a red L COWL A/I DUCT warning. The engine was shut down; an emergency declared and the flight diverted to a nearby airport after the checklist procedures failed to control the pneumatic system.
Two mechanics assigned to defer a #1 engine high stage valve on an A320; inadvertently deactivated the wrong bleed valve in the closed position.

An air carrier deice crew failed to follow company gate deice procedures and began application of deice fluid before the notifying the crew. Deice fluid entered the main cabin door which had not been closed by passenger service in preparation for deicing.
A B747-400 slid and yawed uncontrollably about 120 degrees with the brakes applied as it turned toward its gate on a taxiway in freezing rain.
show: 2009-01 · Ground: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Taxi

text: A B737 with one pack inoperative and cruising at FL250 had the cabin altitude warning horn sound. An emergency was declared with a descent to 15;000 FT where cabin pressurization control was regained when the operating pack was place in high.
CRJ-200 Captain reports a potentially hazardous light pole on short approach to Runway 35 at PHL.

B767 flight crew reports encountering icy taxiway during taxi out at BOS. Brakes and steering are ineffective and reverse thrust is used to stop aircraft and maintain position until help in the form of a super tug can arrive.
show: 2009-01 · Ground: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Taxi

text: A C182 pilot and instructor on a cross country encountered rime ice after making several route adjustments to avoid the weather. On approach to a diversionary airport; the iced over windshield caused approach difficulties.

A Maintenance Inspector reports he may have been involved in the installation of incorrect rivets that were installed as part of an Engineering Order for weight modification improvements on an EMB-145LR; two years earlier.

A B737-800's number one engine failed and caught fire at lift off. Engine failure procedures in mountainous terrain were executed followed by a landing 26 minutes later. The brakes melted during landing requiring that passengers be bussed to the terminal.
show: 2009-01 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Takeoff
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: A 210 HP Glastar 2+2 had an engine failure during a test flight and landed short of a grass airstrip damaging the aircraft's empennage skin near the tail. The fuel injections system was apparently adjusted too richly causing the engine to fail in a nose up attitude.

An ERJ-170 with the number two bleed deferred took off from a mountainous airport and received a 'Bleed 1 Fail' alert. The flight returned for maintenance and was told if the fault cleared after the next takeoff to continue with both bleeds inoperative.

A B737 STAB trim would only trim nose down after takeoff. The STAB Trim Inoperative checklist did not appear to apply. The crew flew with manual trim; declared an emergency and returned to land. Full trim became available on final when configured for landing.

A B747-400 experienced an 'Aileron Lockout' on approach to an airport with winds of 280/18G24 in snow. After troubleshooting and using extra fuel the crew landed with no problems but fatigued after a 12 hour flight on this the sixth day of an international trip.

A large transport air carrier pilot reported nil braking action at the intersection of BUF taxiways 'D' and 'A.' BUF apparently does not use the same snow and ice clearing procedure on taxiways as is used on the runways.
show: 2009-01 · Ground: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Taxi

text: A B747-400 experienced dual FMC failures. The air carrier declared an emergency because of poor destination weather and runway conditions. The crew was able to navigate and fly the approach without problems.

An air carrier pilot crossed the MDW runway 31C hold short line on taxiway E in snow and freezing fog causing an aircraft on approach to go around. The runway was clear but snow covered the taxiway markings.
An air carrier pilot reports a fuel truck crossing in front of his aircraft as he began taxiing at ATL.
Two days after replacing a Primary Flight Display (PFD) on a A320; Mechanic realizes he failed to perform a required CAT-3 check on the aircraft.

A B737-300 was moved between gates during a very cold overnight layover and cockpit air conditioning/heating; electrical and hydraulic systems were configured in an unsafe manner by ground personnel. Equipment damage and human injury were possible.
Regional jet Captain reports low altitude alert from CHS tower during visual approach to Runway 15 during day VMC with the First Officer flying.
B737 Captain describes engine failure occurring during climb through 10.000 FT. Engine is secured and safe return to departure airport ensued. Turbine damage is visible.
Beechcraft Baron pilot is concerned by lack of taxiway identifiers at F45.

A light transport jet pilot was not requested to report a helicopter on short final in sight and in fact did not see it doing a practice hovering autorotation until 100 ft on short final. ATC did not advise the reporter about the traffic's proximity.

An air carrier pilot briefed the complex RDM engine out procedure but failed to brief a normal departure. After takeoff; the crew failed to turn and could not find the transponder identification button to positively identify themselves.
show: 2008-01 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Takeoff

text: B737 Captain reports CSD low oil pressure during final approach. APU is started and generator is put on the bus but CSD is not disconnected. Normal landing ensues with engine shutdown during taxi in.
A320 First Officer reported EGPWS activation just west of XATTU as the aircraft descended to 1;900 FT on visual approach to Runway 10L at SFO. Crew elected to continue and a normal landing ensued.
An air carrier Pilot comments that some Canadian NOTAMS are published in the Canadian system but not in the USA NOTAMS.
B737 Captain describes First Officers attempt to engage the autopilot with 500 FT to go in climb at 4000 FT per minute vertical speed; an Overshoot occured.

A320 Captain reports aircraft pulling strongly to the left as takeoff is commenced. Crew rejects and returns for maintenance. Hot brakes on the left side are noted. Brake and steering control unit reset and brake bleed apparently solved the problem.
Flight Attendant describes events in the cabin after Captain announces a leading edge flap problem. Landing is smooth and safe.

BE350 pilot reports low engine oil pressure at FL180. Reporter elects to shut down the engine and divert for maintenance. An oil line which had recently been replaced during scheduled maintenance was found to be leaking.
An Airbus flight crew experienced ECAM warning BRAKES HOT on takeoff. They consulted with Dispatch and maintenance; declared an emergency; and continued to destination.

PA32 pilot reports destination weather below minimums at the same time it is discovered engine loses power when switched to left tank. Approach to alternate is unsuccessful and Reporters receive vectors to airport with VMC.
ZOB controller described operational deviation when he/she failed to coordinate and ensure aircraft was level prior to adjacent sector as per facility directive.

text: B757-200 flight crew feels signage at intersection of Taxiways E and C at JFK is insufficiently informative.
Mechanic reports flight crew on an A320 could not transfer fuel from center tank. Center tank right pump deferred. Found debris under left pump pickup from contracted overhaul vendor.
The flight crew of a large transport encountered nil braking while taxiing clear of the runway. The Captain elected to shut down and get towed across the icy patch.

text: A11 Controller experienced operational error at approximately 6000 between arrival and departure heavy jets; complicated by restraining runway configuration/capacities and MVA concerns.
A light plane instructor pilot reported hitting a bird that damaged his leading edge. He returned to base safely.
VFR C172 departure from ADS experienced NMAC at 1300 with unreported opposite direction traffic; controller indicated no Mode-C received from Reporter's aircraft.
The pilot of an experimental aircraft reported an engine failure after takeoff. After declaring an emergency he elected to land straight ahead on an unoccupied taxiway.
Air carrier departure from CLT described a go-around event of company aircraft alleging four-digit callsigns caused confusion and the go-around.
