text: A corporate pilot on the SJC9 departure did not realize that a portion of the oak 121 degree radial outbound leg was in sfo class b airspace and required a 200 kt speed restriction and a standard rate turn.
A B737-300 pilot comments about Ramp personnel's failure to clear the gate safety zone of air hoses and a jetway because of insufficiently cleared snow at the last four company destinations.

An ERJ170 First Officer reported being pushed from a gate and contacting the jet bridge with a wing tip. He also reported several deviations from SOP; including no communication with Tug Driver and no lighted wands.
An air carrier pilot questions whether the roc ILS/loc runway 22 requires DME; ADF; and radar. All are required; but the naco chart does not indicate the radar requirement.

An air carrier crew landed on ADQ Runway 25 and found NIL braking after the runway was sand and urea treated. The airport personnel reported the braking action test equipment is not accurate when standing water is on the runway.
An A319 pilot reported he was notified after departure by a Flight Attendant that there were FAMs on board that they were unaware of.

A DHC-8-300 Captain's AHRS failed after takeoff causing the autopilot to disconnect and continue climbing. As the heading drifted; the Captain gave the aircraft to the First Officer and the aircraft was returned to the departure airport. An emergency was not declared.

A B747-400 flight crew departing on a transpacific international flight noticed a thump and abnormal vibration in climb. They consulted with Dispatch and Maintenance; dumped fuel; and returned to departure airport.

A Captain and First Officer report on the apparent discrepancy between the MEL deferral of the #1 Observer's seat to be locked in the stowed position and the crew requirement for the seat to slide to gain access to the circuit breakers behind the seat.

A CRJ200 flight crew experienced a 'smoke toilet' caution message after takeoff and returned to land at departure airport. Pilot Reporter suspects the warning may have been due to deice procedures and glycol in the air conditioning system.
show: 2009-01 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Takeoff
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: A CRJ-200 EICAS alerted 'SMOKE TOILET' at 3;000 FT after takeoff. An emergency was declared with a return to land. The Flight Attendant reported a condensation like cloud that dissipated rapidly. This was the aircraft's third smoke event in three days.
A large transport aircraft on a transpacific flight under CPDLC procedures found out at the end of the flight they had been out of CPDLC contact for some time with no indication of same.
An A319 Captain reported the company procedure for boarding escorts and prisoners was violated because they were not seated in the aircraft's last seating row.
A320 Captain refuses aircraft due to nose wheel steering disconnect button inoperative and MEL'ed.
C150 Instructor with student reports landing in frozen field after unsuccessful attempts to locate VMC airport before darkness. No damage and no injuries reported.
An air carrier pilot comments that some canadian notams published in the canadian system are not in the usa notams.
After deferring the #1 engine CSD/Generator; a Mechanic realizes he failed to sign in the mechanic signature block of the logbook top copy; prior to releasing a Widebody Transport aircraft.
CL65 flight crew declares emergency and returns to land following receipt of at Smoke Toilet alert message.

A light transport jet pilot departed APF on a vector toward HILTI intersection but requested a vector that would keep the aircraft closer to land. ATC requested a phone call after landing to hear the pilot's reason for the request.
Flight crew of a non GPS; FMS equipped MLG suffer a track deviation on takeoff when the FMS fails to provide proper steering information.
A Mechanic is informed he failed to perform a troubleshooting procedure prior to their Maintenance Control issuing an MEL for a deferred item on a B757-200.

A Mechanic is informed that a logbook item he had previously cleared and signed off in their B757-200 logbook for an engine pneumatic problem; had reoccurred; causing an air turnback at a different station.

A Mechanic and Lead Mechanic describe their involvement with the dispatching of a B767-400 aircraft without performing a required CAT-2 and CAT-3 test procedure after swapping the upper and lower EICAS Display Units.
An EMB-140 aborted a takeoff for a flap configuration even though the pre-takeoff check was satisfactory. With the flaps at 9 the flap gauge indicated zero.

An unlicensed Mechanic's Helper and Inspector report on the problems with the opening and closing door handle operation of the forward right service door associated with button head screws on a CRJ-700.
Cessna Turbo 210 pilot fails to switch tanks in a timely fashion and suffers temporary engine failure and altitude/track deviations while recovering.
show: 2009-01 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Cruise

text: An A320's cockpit door hinges were loose; allowing the door bottom to contact the threshold. The door was difficult to close; thus compromising flight station security.
B737 flight crew misunderstood PDC departing SLC and flies WEVIC direct KSINO instead of WEVIC1 KSINO transition. Track deviation occured.
show: 2009-01 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Climb

text: Following a non-precision circling approach to 88J; pilot of a small aircraft experiences NMAC with aircraft landing opposite direction on the same runway.
B737-700 rejects takeoff due to compressor stall. Boroscope shows extensive internal damage.

A Captain of an A319 reports on the lack of experience and knowledge of mechanics; contracted by his carrier; who took three hours to change the #3 main tire; signing off the logbook and leaving the tire under-inflated.
ZID Developmental Controller described operational error at approximately FL300; during crossing traffic/descent event; claiming Mode-C altitude swap as a contributing factor.

A Captain describes the events that led to his refusal of a B777-200 for a cabin door slide/raft arming lever that was frozen in the 'armed' position. Problem caused by water intrusion into the door and freezing the arming lever.
Lavatory fire alarm strong chemical odors near an aft lavatory resulted in an emergency declaration and return to departure airport.
HS125 stopped abruptly while taxiing to avoid a ground vehicle passing in front of them at high speed.

SF340 returned to departure airport following a Smoke Toilet caution message and reported 'mist and/or condensation' in the vicinity of the aft lavatory. Aircraft had two previous write-ups of Smoke Toilet warnings in the previous two days.

text: A First Officer on an EMB 145 reports that during climb out; a loud squeal was heard coming from one of the Captain's windows. On descent the loud noise returned. Maintenance found all but 8 screws that held the windscreen in place were loose.

Captain reports he noticed his statement of 'aircraft refused' had been deleted from the rest of the electronic maintenance log entry he made for a B777-200 inoperative door slide arming lever and improper alignment of the girt bar engaged flags on the same door.
G200 captain reports exceeding 1500 ft restriction at wentz on the ruudy1 RNAV departure from teb.

text: CRJ200 landed under emergency conditions when the steering inop warning is displayed upon gear extension.
Air Carrier departure from IAD; with similar four digit call sign as previous departure; initiated wrong initial heading; claiming similar call signs as casual.
SF340 flight crew encounters engine bleed and pneumatic system CWP warning messages and decide to return to departure airport for maintenance.
New A320 Captain's unfamiliarity with the fleet's TCAS system contributes to the need to respond to a TCAS RA on approach to parallel runways.
A mechanic and Maintenance Inspector report on the events that contributed to a CRJ-200 APU battery being installed in a CRJ-900.

Two Mechanics report not resetting the circuit breakers for the fuel override jettison pumps and not performing a required fuel pump operational check. The B767-300 returned to field after takeoff with boost pump messages.
A320 diverted to nearest suitable airport following completion of Quick Reference Checklist checklists for an ECAM 'Engine Reverser 2 Pressurized' message.

B757-200 flight crew experienced failure of the left engine drive hydraulic pump along with a status message regarding the Power Transfer Unit; a hydraulic system abnormal configuration facilitator. Declared emergency for an eventual uneventful landing at their destination.
B757-200 flight crew receives 'trailing edge flap disagreement' EICAS message. Perform go-around; conduct appropriate checklists; declare emergency and land uneventfully.
A B767-300 Captain reports on a problem with the right center fuel pump. After ten days of troubleshooting; a connector pin was found miswired.
A First Officer describes the chain of events that led to mechanics servicing the crew oxygen bottle for the Saab 340B with passengers onboard.

A line mechanic reports their B777-200 cabin door slide arming cable freezes; preventing the arming or disarming of the door. His carrier has an engineering repair procedure for their fleet to address the freezing cable problem; which allegedly has not been accomplished.

Pilot of B737-300 reported noting rime ice on the leading edge of the horizontal stabilizer during the walkaround. While advising Deicing Control he received a report from the deicing crew that the airplane was free of ice.
CRJ200 Captain reports FLAPS FAIL EICAS with flaps at 8 degrees. QRH is consulted and safe landing ensues.
CRJ200 Check Captain comments positively on the operating crews' handling of a wing anti-ice malfunction; and suggests SOP might be changed to require ground testing under more circumstances.
CE680 Captain reports cabin door being opened from the outside with the aircraft slightly pressurized. Door suspension is damaged and injury narrowly avoided.

A Lead Mechanic describes a chain of events that culminated with a fuel spill during the refueling of a B757-200 after the aircraft had arrived with many deferrals; three of them related to the fuel system; but inaccurately recorded in the aircraft's maintenance log.
B737-800 Captain reports ill passenger during arrival and asymmetrical flaps during approach. QRH is complied with while doctor attends to passenger. Safe landing ensues.
show: 2009-01 · Flight Deck: Illness / Injury · Initial Approach

text: B767 Captain reports EGT failure during climbout. Crew elects to return to departure airport for an overweight landing.
Following a loud bang; vibration and flash from the #1 engine; a B737-700 crew rejected the takeoff at about 110 KTS and declared an emergency. Crash/Fire/Rescue examined the aircraft.

SF340 flight crew experienced; on departure; a loud 'flapping' noise accompanied by an overtemp warning on the number one engine. A precautionary engine shutdown was completed; emergency declared and a uneventful return to landing was accomplished.

An air carrier at 2300 ft on an intercept heading for the BUF ILS Runway 23 pitched up to 30 degrees and climbed 1400 ft as it approached the ILS glideslope from the north. The aircraft was at flaps 5 degrees and 190 kt but slowed to 120 kts during the 20 second event.

B747-400 flight crew reported on the maintenance practices of an international contracted maintenance provider; trying to get them to accept a Maintenance Release; prior to completing the nose strut servicing and the gear doors being closed.

After applying an MEL 28-3A for a fault with the low pressure light for the right forward fuel boost pump on a B737-400; a Maintenance Controller is later informed a pressure switch had been identified; even though no one had done any troubleshooting.

A loose oil line to a PA-46 oil pressure transducer caused a loss of torque during climb. The engine was shut down at 11;000 FT and the pilot glided to a power off landing at his departure airport. An emergency was not declared.
A PA-32 engine's crankshaft broke in flight at 7;000 FT. The pilot declared an emergency with ATC and landed at a nearby airport.

A B757 cabin crew detected a strong electrical smell at cruise. The SMOKE/FUME Checklist as well as personal electronic devices were turned off. The smell dissipated until on final approach when the crew declared an emergency because of the smell's return.

Upon arriving at the gate; a B777-200 flight crew discover cabin door 4-right 'arm/disarm' lever and door handle were malfunctioning. 	with no reference to door problem in the maintenance release. Captain refuses aircraft.

While deicing a CRJ-200; a Ground crew member's hand became caught in the flap causing a 'Flaps Fail' indication. The pilots were not advised until after emergency responders arrived that someone was injured.

A PA-60-600 was given a go-around when he was unable to maintain power to increased approach speed because of erratic fuel flow possibly due to contamination or extreme cold. The pilot declared an emergency on the next approach.

A light transport jet got a TCAS 'Traffic; Traffic' alert while on a visual downwind to ADS Runway 33. ATC did not call the traffic; but the flight crew had visual contact with it less than 500 FT below them.

A CRJ-200 crew experienced smoke in the cockpit; the lavatory smoke alarms sounded and a Flight Attendant reported cabin smoke. This occurred shortly after air conditioning bleeds were selected to APU from engine. An emergency was declared.
B777 Captain wonders why international airports don't have runway grooving information on the back of the airport diagram as is common for domestic airports.
An air carrier pilot comments that some Canadian NOTAMS are published in the Canadian system but not in the USA NOTAMS.

text: An A320 aircraft slid off a taxiway in nil braking conditions after exiting the runway onto an extremely icy; downhill sloped taxiway.
PA34 pilot reports runaway electric trim at 6000 ft. Control of aircraft is lost until trim motor circuit breaker trips.

text: After troubleshooting and finding the right pack fan inoperative on an MD-80; a Mechanic notices the replacement fan part number on the Airworthiness Release 8130 tag; was different from the part number on the fan data plate.
A SF340's right generator failed at cruise. An emergency was declared followed by an emergency landing.

An air carrier pilot taxiing in low visibility on taxiway 'b' to ramp position 55; exited taxiway 'b' at taxiway spot 6 and discovered the aircraft at ramp spot 66. The commercial airport chart appears to depict taxiway spot 6 incorrectly.

Captain reports diverting his Cessna 560 Citation Ultra due to lack of crew oxygen from his and the First Officer's oxygen masks. Captain also notices a hissing sound coming from his mask both in-flight and after landing.

A DHC8-400 (Q-400) #2 PEC light illuminated during the climb after takeoff. The propeller oversped and the engine was shut down. An emergency was declared with an emergency landing at a nearby airport.

A Mechanic returns to an A320 after previously positioning a ladder in the right wheel well and notices the aircraft had settled onto the ladder from the loading of fuel; passengers and baggage; causing damage to the wheel well fairing.

While performing a preflight on the same A320 he flew in the night before; a Captain reports the overnight contract maintenance mechanics had signed off the Maintenance Release; but failed to close and latch two panels; which included the Integrated Drive Generator servicing panel on #2 engine nacelle.

A B737-NG Flight Attendant opened the L1 door with the slide armed after being distracted by other crew communications. The slide did not deploy because the Captain assisted putting the slide pack back in the casing.

A PA-28 instructor pilot declared an emergency in order to receive an immediate approach clearance ahead of an air carrier because his aircraft began collecting ice. The PA-28 did not have de-ice equipment.
A BE-58 pilot declared an emergency and descended to a lower altitude while flying IFR and accumulating ice on his anti-icing equipped aircraft.
Distracted by a mis-set transponder code; flight crew of DA50 fail to maintain 1500 ft MSL on TEB SID from TEB.
show: 2009-01 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Initial Climb

text: A Mechanic reports about transposing the wrong B737-700 tail number when verifying with Maintenance Control if he had the correct part for a log book write-up of a weak #1 VHF. He installed a #1 VDR not effective for the aircraft.
While attempting to connect an electrical cord from a GPU to a B737-700; a Technician notices the GPU had short circuited.
An IFR PA-27 pilot lost electrical power during climb out and could not talk with ATC or squawk transponder codes. The pilot returned to land at his departure airport NORDO.
CL604 flight crew fail to comply with 1500 foot restriction on the RUUDY SID off TEB.
show: 2009-01 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Initial Climb

text: An EMB-145 pilot reports that after repeated maintenance entries for a loud noise from the Captain's windows; maintenance found numerous loose screws in the Captain's forward windshield.
VFR C210 with ZTL requested IFR descent through cloud layer; canceled IFR after VMC; but later confused flight status; IFR vs. VFR during continued descent.

A B737 pilot notes large amounts of ice and snow in both engine's inlets during preflight. The ice had frozen the fans and ground air was used to thaw the ice where de-ice fluid may damage engine components.

A Mechanic documenting discrepancies on a B737-500 did not realize three sequenced form numbers (non-routines) were removed from the stack they were using; and incorrectly entered them on the tally sheet for an 'A' check.
PA28 with gear problem elected to return to departure airport; ATC declared emergency and issued go-around to parallel runway traffic; reporter may have crossed hold line.
MD90 Captain reports blown tire after landing on snow covered runway with max auto brakes set.

An ERJ170 flight crew experienced high oil consumption and low oil quantity during their flight and wrote it up inbound. The reporter expressed some concern about the company's handling of the write up.

The lavatory smoke detectors on a B757-200 all alarmed during an engine start using an external air cart because the air entering the cabin was polluted by exhaust from nearby equipment. The aircraft was evacuated at the gate while the smoke source was determined.
show: 2009-01 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Parked
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: A B757 responded to an EGPWS on the TUS Runway 11L localizer when they descended below 5500 FT outside of CALLS Intersection on a night visual approach. The ILS glide slope was NOTAM'ed inoperable.
show: 2009-01 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Initial Approach

text: Dispatched with the FMS inoperative; flight crew of ERJ are cleared direct to a VOR which is NOTAM'd out of service and must learn for themselves they can't navigate to it.
A B737-800 with an asymmetrical flap warning on approach. An emergency was declared followed by a landing after completing the appropriate checklists.
An air carrier pilot notes a common misconception about Type IV anti-ice fluid application prior to a day's flight can contaminate the wing and must be removed with Type I fluid.
MD11 Captain reports receiving Battery Discharging alert at FL310 and diverts to the nearest suitable airport as required by Flight Manual.
B737-300 Captain reports Maintenance falsely reported a log book discrepancy as having been repaired. After refusing the false Maintenance Release; a Technician defers the item.
Fuelers failed to properly install fuel cap.
B717 Captain experiences a compressor stall on departure with engine continuing to operate normally after the event. Crew elects to return for uneventful landing.
C182 instructor reports that G1000 MFD/PFD brightness control knob functions opposite to that indicated by graphic printed around the knob.
C172 pilot reports aircraft damage after taxiing into culvert in the south Ramp at FMY. Ramp lighting in the area is inoperative.
C182 pilot attempts takeoff on short taxiway thinking he is on the runway when takeoff clearance is received. Tower calls abort too late to prevent going across parallel runway into grass.
CL65 Captain reports hot start during attempted cross bleed start. Hot icon and flames and smoke report from aircraft behind cause start to be aborted.
show: 2009-01 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Taxi
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: Mechanic reports he installed incorrect annulus fillers during the fan blade reinstallation on the #2 engine of a B757-200.
E190 pilot reports cockpit opening on takeoff. He believes that this may be a recurring problem.
BE33 pilot reports alternator failure during a VFR cross country flight. Flight ends well with the aid of ATC and an airline crew.
A wake turbulence encounter behind a preceding Airbus causes a B737 to temporarily abandon a special noise abatement departure procedure in order to recover.
show: 2009-01 · Inflight: Wake Vortex Encounter · Initial Climb

text: A B737 encounters wake turbulence several times during arrival in trail of a B767 beginning at FL240 and ending at 4000 ft.
Dispatcher is informed by MD11 crew that Battery Discharging alert that had previously caused two diversions has reappeared but the crew is continuing to destination.
Air carrier flight crew report communications difficulties with MDT Ground after landing and critical conflict with EMB110 during taxi to gate.

A G1159A (GIII) pressurization control panel failed at FL270. An emergency descent followed but ATC could not hear the pilot because of cockpit noise. The problem was traced to the pressurization control panel canon plug.
PA46 pilot reports HSI failure during departure and reversion to hand flying and visual separation from terrain. Deviations from SID occurred and ATC notified of the failure.
show: 2009-01 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Climb

text: A balloon pilot landing at Tracy; CA; Airport comments that some fixed wing pilots do not realize the difficulty balloon pilots have preparing to land near an airport when a conflict with a fixed wing aircraft develops.
Two B767 Flight Attendants report a severe turbulence encounter lasting nearly one hour on an oceanic trip. Proper crew preparation prevented injury or damage.
EMB145 flight crew reports encountering icy taxiway after landing and is unable to continue. Aircraft is towed to the gate and no damage occurs.
show: 2009-01 · Ground: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Taxi

text: EMB170 flight crew reports declaring a fuel emergency during approach due to ATC delays. Initial response to declaration is 'Roger.' Crew eventually receives vectors to a different runway.

SF340 First Officer reports compressor stall and autocoarsen event during departure. As Captain commences engine failure memory items; engine returns to normal operation. Crew continues to destination.
B767 Captain reports rejected takeoff just after 80 knot call for possible engine failure and momentary loss of directional control.
show: 2009-01 · Ground: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Takeoff

text: A FA-20 pilot back-taxied on a CTAF airport's runway because he was unfamiliar with the taxiways and was nearly hit by a landing G-IV. It was a night operation and the airport was IMC with a one-half a mile visibility.

C172 instructor reports NMAC with PA28 during night visual approach from the traffic pattern. PA28 pilot; who is below and behind; and does not make a base turn call. Another C172 pilot makes 360 degree turn on final to avoid the PA28.

CRJ900 First Officer reports in-flight shut down for low oil pressure after the engine driven hydraulic pump had been replaced just prior to departure. Post flight inspection revealed the pump had been improperly installed allowing the engine oil to leak.

ZNY Controller witnessed loss of separation when a military flight requested breakup; multiple destination changes; and then declared an emergency; resulting in an operational error. Limited airspace and distractions listed as casual factors.
A light aircraft conducting flight training experienced an NMAC with a light twin in the pattern at DAB.

A B737-300 flight crew experienced loss of cabin pressure. They declared an emergency; descended; coordinated with dispatch; and diverted to a nearby airport. The crew experienced confusion about the warning horn's meaning.

A B757-200 flight crew in cruise experienced loss of left hydraulic system followed by loss of PTU (power transfer unit). They ran the checklists; declared an emergency; and landed at their destination.

An ERJ-170 departed after a delay for a foul smell but declared an emergency and returned to land because of a forward cargo door open EICAS message. The door had previously been MEL'ed but the crew missed the MEL note.

An air carrier pilot comments that after having been deiced at ZZZ; the next airport ground crew found ice on the horizontal stabilizer and other aircraft parts because they were not properly deice prior to departure. Infrequent deice operations and darkness are factors.
A Director of Maintenance describes the confusion in their maintenance tracking program for their Cessna Caravan-208B; where all six flap tracks exceeded the inspection time limit requirement.

After an off-airport landing because of a partial power loss; an RV6A pilot found that the aircraft's Operational Limitations document was not with the aircraft as required for amateur build experimental aircraft.

MCO Controller experienced loss of separation when distracted by weather deviations in another part of the sector; believing they had issued an interim separation altitude; but had not issued any altitude restriction.

An R22 B11 departed with the electronic fuel quantity indicators showing half full tanks. Approximately three minutes into the flight both tank gauges indicated low fuel. A precautionary off airport landing was completed. Inaccurate fuel guages are suspected.
MD80 cabin attendants encountered smoke in the cabin shortly after takeoff. Advised the flight crew who returned to the departure airport.
show: 2008-12 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Initial Climb
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: ATR72 flight crew suffered a left engine failure accompanied by smoke and audible indications of engine damage.
show: 2009-01 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Cruise
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: Flight crew of ATR72 returned to departure airport when the right main gear failed to retract after takeoff.
Cabin Attendants evacuate passengers out the jetway due to smoke in the cabin. One passenger chooses to ignore their commands; preferring to continue a search for a missing cell phone.
IFR departure attempting to contact NCT was issued low altitude alert; later discovering ATC had issued wrong clearance; an operational error was recorded.
CE525 pilot reports TAWS warning departing VNY to the south at 1700 FT and commences climb and left turn.
show: 2009-01 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Initial Climb

text: CRJ Captain reports electrical fumes at FL300 during climb. Oxygen masks are donned and clearance for descent and diversion are obtained from Center. At 10000 FT no fumes are present and normal landing ensues.
show: 2009-01 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Climb
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: CRJ200 Captain reports fuel spill after fueler attempts to pressure refuel aircraft that has this system on MEL.

A319 pilot reports transient nose wheel steering fault during pushback then after 4 hours in cruise a landing gear shock absorber fault. This is followed shortly by autopilot; auto throttle; and Flight Director failures. Descending through 10;000 FT all systems are regained and normal landing ensues.

A pilot receiving a CFI practical check ride was given a simulated engine failure that led to a simulated emergency approach to a nearby airport. While correcting a high final approach altitude; the Reporter failed to lower the landing gear.
MIA Local Controller described operational error; during an attempt to establish visual separation with two closely spaced arrival aircraft; go-around issued but automation review detected error.
Air carrier landing at AMA described heavy separation event when ATC directed military aircraft to turn resulting in the subject over flight situation.
show: 2009-01 · ATC Issue All Types · Initial Approach

text: A B737-NG cabin climbed to 10000 ft while in cruise at FL340. The Captain timidly began an emergency descent. The cabin reached 12000 ft while the First Officer executed a high rate of descent to FL240 where the cabin stabilized at 8000 ft. Maintenance found the outflow valve frozen with leaking cabin system water.
Small aircraft on departure roll; observed aircraft crossing runway down field; elected to maximize climb and over fly incursion traffic; causing a pilot deviation.

As a JFK air carrier ground crew pushed an aircraft from its gate; a wing tip struck the horizontal stabilizer of an aircraft on the same terminal. The alleyway was very wide where both aircraft were located.
An A320 flight crew got low and slow on a night visual to TPA; the First Officer noticed the speed brakes were still extended.

A Flight Design CTRS does not display the status of the autopilot engagement and when the autopilot is engaged the aircraft is difficult to control. When landing the engine emergency light illuminated with reduced rpm and one wing tank was found empty.

Shortly after passing MANNI on the ILS Rwy 12 at BZN; air carrier flight crew fails to level at MAP altitude when a go-around is initiated due to an autopilot pitch-up in response to an anomalous full up glide slope indication.

Cleared to YOQMU IAF for the RNAV Runway 24 approach at ARB; pilot of C172 misunderstands and proceeds direct to YACNU; an IAF for the RNAV Runway 24 approach; citing difficulty in distinguishing the difference when the two words are spoken.
show: 2009-01 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Cruise

text: While enroute; a Captain and First Officer realized their B757-200 was placarded under the wrong Minimum Equipment List (MEL) option 32-7a. MEL should have been 32-7b; 'Auto Brakes light Illuminated; Switch OFF;' requiring maintenance check. Aircraft diverted.
A light transport corporate aircraft crew descended early on a BTR RWY 4L RNAV approach because of FMS programming distractions and the lack of procedure familiarity.

Two pilots report on a rudder bias malfunction that occurred during two taxi out checks on their company Cessna 560XL. The First Officer did not notice the rudder pedal movement was opposite of that intended; during their first taxi out check.

An A319 had multiple EWD faults starting with a 'WHEEL NW STRG FAULT' on pushback. In flight 'ICE STBY PITOT' and 'L/G SHOCK ABSORBER FAULT' alerted; then dual FMGC and flight director failures. All indications returned to normal on descent but an emergency was declared.

During a walkaround of a B777-200 at an international station; a relief First Officer noticed a Mechanic wiping fuel from the bottom of the wing just inboard of the left engine. Contract Maintenance wanted to classify the fuel leak as a stain; which would allow dispatch of the aircraft; Captain refused.
A CRJ700 flight crew experienced GEAR DISAGREE CAS alert on approach. They ran the QRH; manually extended the gear; did a fly-by for visual confirmation; and landed normally.
A B757-200 Captain reported that during defueling executed by a fuel vendor he observed a number of deviations from procedure.
An SR22 pilot departing TEB climbed through the charted altitude when distracted by an over-boost condition.
IFR corporate aircraft landing APF experienced TCAS RA with ATC reported traffic; traffic not sighted until RA maneuver.
An MD90 flight crew experienced uncommanded shutdown of their one running engine during single engine taxi.
An MD80 flight crew experienced zero pack airflow during climb. They ran the procedures but never regained normal flow; so they returned to their departure airport.
A B757-200 flight crew experienced high vibration levels on the right engine. They coordinated with Dispatch and Maintenance; declared an emergency; and returned to their departure airport.

A C182 pilot landed in a 16 kt crosswind; ballooned then contacted the right wing tip and propeller on the second touch down. The maximum tested crosswind landing was 15 kts. Actual crosswind was a 60 degrees cross gusting to 25 kts.
A VFR Europa and a Beech Baron had a near miss as the Europa descended through 2700 FT on the edge of Class D to its home field and the Beech was passing through the adjacent Class D at 2600 FT.
show: 2009-01 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Descent

text: A PA-24 on a break-in test flight after cylinder changes; ran out of fuel and glided into a nearby Class C airport. The aircraft had a fuel line leak and the fuel flow was unusually high because of the new engine components.
SCT controller described separation event at 4500 FT with LAX arrival and overflight aircraft; resulting from missed incorrect altitude assignment readback.
ZID Controller experienced operational error at FL320 involving three aircraft that resulted from an incorrect altitude clearance readback that was missed.

An air carrier crew's ICAO formatted DFW NOBLY3 LIT RNAV PDC was different from the old format. The new ICAO format led the crew to believe direct LIT was correct when the new format actually required full route compliance.
show: 2009-02 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Climb

text: A B1900 departed with insufficient fuel. Flight crew failed to verify the fuel on board with the fuel slip.

A Flight Attendant heard an unusual noise in the aircraft's aft area during flight that was investigated after arrival. Nothing unusual was found but during the next flight the aircraft diverted for a hydraulic pump problem.
A Mechanic reports he was misinformed by his acting Lead Mechanic and did not have a RII accomplished after changing the #3 Main Landing Gear brake on a B757-200.

A B737-700 was deiced with Type I fluid before leaving an overnight station at dawn. At the next station they were told ice still adhered to the wings near the spoiler and the horizontal stabilizer. The aircraft was deiced before departure.
ZTL controller described TCAS RA event at FL250 likely caused by the rapid descent of one of the two aircraft involved; separation was retained.

An HS125-800 pilot turned the digital electronic engine control (SYNCH) switch off at 600 ft after takeoff causing an over temp. the SYNCH switch is a three position switch next to an identical engine synchronizer switch which the pilot intended to turn on.

A light transport jet crew assigned a 240 degrees heading on the SLC 9 departure was unable to contact SLC on a congested tower frequency and so contacted TRACON without ATC instructions as they headed toward mountainous terrain.

An air carrier at 2500 ft 5 miles from BUF on an ILS Runway 23 localizer intercept heading from the north pitched up 18 degrees and climbed to 3000 ft. A rapid power application to counter the slowing airspeed contributed to the pitch up and 10 kt airspeed loss.

A CE560XLS flight crew experienced STAB MISCOMPARE; HYD PRESS; and L MLG UNLOCK lights after selecting gear down while flaps were in transit. They blew the gear down; declared an emergency; and diverted to a more suitable airport.
An A320 pilot comments that CRT readability is decreased during bright ambient light conditions. The air carrier maintenance did not replace the unreadable CRT.
B737 Captain discovers in flight that the CVR written up and MELed is listed as a FDR on the Dispatch Release.
A B737 NG flight crew experienced total radio failure in cruise flight. They intermittently had use of the radios; and got landing clearance at their destination.
With the First Officer; Reporter; heads down conducting the Before Takeoff Checklist and the Captain preoccupied performing a rudder system check; their Cessna 560 encroached on the active runway.
After clearing Runway 4R on K at HNL; an air carrier failed to hold short of Runway 8L as cleared.

SF340 flight crew noted fumes in the cockpit shortly after departure followed shortly thereafter by a R INTAKE caution light. Procedures were followed and the fumes dispersed shortly thereafter; followed by an uneventful return the their departure airport.
show: 2009-02 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Climb
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: An A320 flight crew experienced a track deviation on the BARIN 1 RNAV arrival to IAD when the FMGC entered the DECES transition to the ILS Runway 1R vice flying to BARIN and thence radar vectors per the procedure.
show: 2009-02 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Initial Approach

text: Air carrier Captain advises NOTAMS for BUF contained an Internet web site referenced rather than coded information. Attempts to access any information regarding the NOTAM proved fruitless.

Departure Controller notes the failure of pilots departing SDL to abide with change to initial climb clearance via BANYO and SCOTTSDALE SIDs. Controller believes SIDS should have been revised when arrival route was changed to avoid procedure conflict.
CL604 failed to capture the 336 radial out of PXR on the SCOT5 SID from SDL.
show: 2009-01 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Initial Climb

text: A B737-700 flight crew on approach to ATL deviated from track and altitude assignments; in part due to their lack of familiarity with Primary Flight Display symbology.
show: 2009-01 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Initial Approach

text: B737 Flight Attendant is informed during preflight that the flight deck door lock is MEL'ed and can only be unlocked manually by the pilots from the flight deck.
A B757 flight crew and cabin crew noticed a plastic smell. The flight crew declared an emergency and diverted to the nearest suitable airport.
show: 2009-02 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Cruise
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: A pilot of an experimental light aircraft experienced an NMAC on short final to GVQ when a low wing light aircraft passed him 20 FT overhead.
Air carrier Captain describes a situation where a jumpseat occupant severs his fingertip in the footrest of the B757 cockpit jumpseat.
A Maintenance Manager reports he was informed by a Mechanic stationed at a de-icing pad; who observed aircraft being deiced with fluid improperly heated to 120F degrees; less than required.

Both of a B757's engines were damaged by FOD after landing at JAC on a runway clear of snow and ice. The runway clearing machine was removing the asphalt surface leaving pebbles to damage the aircraft's engines.
An A320 flight crew deviated from their assigned course when their FMC dropped out some points on the BARIN arrival to IAD.
show: 2009-02 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Initial Approach

text: A CRJ200 flight crew experienced LANDING GEAR DISAGREE warning after takeoff. They ran the checklist; declared an emergency and returned to their departure airport; where they found the left main landing gear was still pinned.
A CRJ200 Captain reported running an engine on the ground after maintenance and his jet blast overturned and damaged a tug crossing behind him.
Right engine of a B757-200 ingested an eagle on climbout. Returned under emergency declaration.
An A319 pilot comments that CRT readability is decreased during bright ambient light conditions. The air carrier maintenance did not replace the unreadable CRT.
Pilot of PA46 Malibu lost control on landing and exited runway collapsing nose gear and striking prop in a snow bank. An Airworthiness Directive has been issued for the PA46 steering.

DA20 Captain reports rejected takeoff for sliding window opening on the roll. During taxi back on taxiway Q a communication lapse with Ground causes Tower to order a go around to traffic landing Runway 1C.
Cessna 182 pilot suffered loss of communication due to alternator failure. Returned to departure airport.
Instructor and student pilots of a C172RG lose control on landing due to a right brake leak.
show: 2009-02 · Ground: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Landing

text: Pilot reports taxi conflict with CRJ exiting Runway 30R. Ground Control had not given any instructions and the reporter chose to detour slightly around the CRJ and continue down taxiway P. The Reporter stated that the Ground Controller was looking directly into the rising sun and did not give timely instructions to either aircraft.
Citation departing PRC described conflict event; reaching V1 speed a light aircraft was observed crossing the departure runway down field.
C152 instructor reports go-around on very short final when another instructional aircraft appears likely to enter the runway. Tower issues go-around moments later.
Three Mechanics and an Inspector are informed about an EMB-145 Captain's windshield shattering and their involvement with the window removal and installation; that occurred months earlier.
Widebody Captain is instructed to cross Runway 36C on Kilo but stops at red hold bars and questions Tower. Reporter is instructed to ignore the hold bars and cross Runway 36C on Kilo.
A DHC8-300 elevator became too stiff to allow rotation at takeoff speed after the aircraft was anti-iced with type 4 fluid; possibly creating an 'air dam' at the leading edge of the elevator.
show: 2009-02 · Ground: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Takeoff

text: B757 Captain reports cabin altitude warning at FL390. QRH procedures are complied with and crew elects to divert for maintenance.

A320 flight crew reports sensor faults on both engines during takeoff roll at moderate speed and rejects the takeoff. Aircraft had spent the night in sub-zero temperatures and freezing fog and was deiced prior to departure.
B747 Captain reports L2 cockpit window delamination that Maintenance is reluctant to repair prior to departure; citing erroneous information concerning the L1 window.
B757 Captain reports rejecting takeoff for cabin door message at around 100 knots.
BE90 First Officer reports Captain's side window failure at FL210 and decision to divert to nearest suitable airport.
C172 student and instructor report rejected takeoff after conflict with helicopter; when pilot apparently accepted their takeoff clearance on an intersecting runway.
M20 pilot reports throttle linkage failure with throttle fixed at high power setting. When landing is assured engine is shut down with mixture control. Safe landing ensues.
A Mechanic reports he may have failed to comply with a procedure contained in the Configuration Deviation List (CDL) for a B757-200; with an air conditioning door latch locking feature not secured.

As a boarding passenger attempted to utilize his cane to rise from his wheel chair at the aircraft door his cane slipped between the jetway and the jet; causing him to fall and injuring a Cabin Attendant who attempted to break his fall.
Cabin attendant discovered an overheating water heater when responding to a lavatory smoke alarm. Maintenance failed to resolve the problem.
Two air carriers described TCAS RA go-around event during visual approach maneuvers to parallel runways; suggesting questionable ATC handling.
BE400 Captain reports heading deviation departing DFW runway 18L due to compass system malfunction. Strong winds aloft were also reported.
show: 2009-02 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Initial Climb

text: B737 returned to departure airport due to reports of chemical smells in the cabin.
show: 2009-02 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Climb
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: Captain reports about B737-300 autothrottles (A/T) having trouble holding adequate thrust for cruise mach. Disconnected the autothrottles and noticed the #1 engine throttle would not manually move past the mid position (80% N1 at cruise).
First Officer of CRJ aircraft reported flaps failed to retract following takeoff. The Flight Crew performed the appropriate Quick Reference Handbook procedures and returned to the departure airport.
Cleared only to the transition altitude departing EGLL; B767-300 flight crew set QNE prematurely and leveled off nearly 800 feet low due to the low altimeter setting.
First Officer of an unidentified aircraft type reported the rubber deposits on the ungrooved runways at MMMX compromise braking effectiveness when wet.
MIA Local Controller witnessed loss of wake turbulence separation when adjacent Local Controller vectored departure aircraft behind heavy without proper spacing.
Grumman AA-5 may have entered Class C while experiencing a NMAC with another aircraft.
MD88 suffered a total loss of pressurization at FL340. Made emergency descent to 9000 MSL and continued to destination.
A MD-80 fuel system would only feed from the right main tank and not from the center tank as configured. An emergency was declared with a return to land.
HUF Controller described deviation event when issuing a non standard altitude and then failing to point out traffic to an adjacent sector; claiming others duties caused momentary inattention.
A CE650 flight crew climbed through the charted altitude on departure out of TEB.
A small aircraft pilot reports striking an unmarked pole with a wing tip. The pole is located about two feet from the edge of a ramp.

Terrain warnings resulted when an MD88 flight crew departed ABQ with incorrect interpretation of the voluntary noise abatement procedure delineated by the several publications -- company and federally -- provided for their use.

IFR Citation landing HND; vectored by L30 TRACON; experienced conflict at 6300 with issued VFR traffic; executed emergency climb; Reporter claiming ATC's decision to issue decent clearance into known traffic was a safety issue.
Mechanic was informed of an air return of a B737-500 caused by a bent pin on the connector of the autopilot servo. Incident happened six weeks after he replaced the horizontal stabilizer jackscrew.

Mechanic reports he found 7x8 inch delamination on a B757-200 radome at the three o'clock position. Aircraft was released after evaluating damage with Engineering. An FAA inspector questioned the signoff procedure.

Instructor pilot of C172 on short final was distressed at the insensitivity of the pilot of another aircraft who turned on the pilot controlled lighting to full intensity at PBG. Acts irresponsibly by announcing 'flash blindness' had caused his aircraft to crash and flip over in a snow bank.
ZID Controller experienced operational error at 11;000 FT when overtake event was not recognized in time for corrective action to be effective.
Light aircraft pilot arriving FDK reports critical conflict during crosswind turn with another aircraft departing Runway 23 and turning west.

A Mechanic assigned to perform an ETOPS check and walk around on a B777 with heavy snow accumulation; requests the aircraft be de-iced; to avoid an incomplete visual inspection. His carrier does not have a written policy on de-icing aircraft prior to ETOPS inspections.

A Mechanic involved with building up and packing MD-80 Tailcone Evacuation slides; reports he was not provided with a packing tool required to the pack slide assemblies; per their Engineering Order and Component Maintenance Manual.
EMB145 First Officer reports LAV SMOKE EICAS at FL240 and diversion to nearest suitable airport.

SF340 Captain reports hydraulic master caution and unsafe gear during approach. After complying with checklist procedures flight returns for landing. During rollout left engine auto coarsens momentarily when reverse is selected. Normal taxi to gate.

B757-200 Captain is informed by Ramp personnel that cargo doors will not operate. Maintenance is called and utility busses are cycled to correct the problem. Reporter does not understand this fix and requests more documentation.
While in cruise; CRJ200 Captain reports amber 'STAB TRIM' and 'MACH TRIM' CAS messages. After complying with QRH procedures crew diverts to nearest suitable airport.
B717 First Officer reports symptoms of possible carbon monoxide poisoning experienced by passengers and cabin crew on two segment flight. On second leg Captain elects to divert for medical attention.
Captain of an A320 refuses to accept Maintenance Release for his aircraft that was prepared in advance of the work having been performed.
B767 Cabin Attendants discover at the end of their flight that Federal Air Marshals were aboard; unknown to any of the crew.
An A319 pilot comments that CRT readability is decreased during bright ambient light conditions. The air carrier maintenance did not replace the unreadable CRT.
Two Mechanics report how the right aft overwing slide door opened and the slide came out; but did not deploy; after they replaced the slide door sensor on a B767-300.
ZAN controller described event where supervisory actions during sector de-combination resulted in an unexpected loss of frequency; setting up a potential loss of separation.

AUS Approach Controller described technical loss of separation when they failed to issue visual approach wake turbulence advisory after trailing air carrier reported heavy traffic in sight and following.
show: 2009-02 · ATC Issue All Types · Initial Approach

text: C172 pilot plans VFR flight and receives weather brief for VMC along the route of flight. Low ceilings and icing conditions are encountered causing the declaration of emergency and vectors to the nearest airport by ATC.

L30 Controller described an operational deviation event when adjacent controller issued approach clearance without the required point out; resulting in the Tower assigning a runway change for one arrival aircraft.
show: 2008-12 · Airspace Violation All Types · Initial Approach

text: B737-400 Captain reports APU fire warning at FL320 during climb. Fire handle is pulled and agent is discharged in accordance with QRH procedures. Flight diverts to nearest suitable airport.
Captain reported a superfluous RAAS warning regarding approaching the runway to which they had been cleared interfered with the Tower's clearance to cross the runway.
Captain of unidentified air carrier type aircraft is advised after the fact that the MEL regarding the engine igniter system on his aircraft was in error.
Air carrier landing SFO with fuel concerns voiced concern regarding NCT handling; recommending continued holding in lieu of extensive vectoring for sequence.
show: 2009-02 · ATC Issue All Types · Initial Approach

R44 helicopter pilot reported striking a bird during a sightseeing flight.

Mechanic reports he was notified he had installed an engine fuel pump for a -3 engine; on a -5 engine; eight months earlier; on one of their B757-200s.

C310 pilot was surprised by deer on the runway following a night landing.

After test flying and ferrying a Bell 206-L1 (LongRanger-2) evacuation helicopter; following a main transmission change; pilot is informed the transmission was not registered and the aircraft had flown three more times prior to being grounded.

Two Mechanics are informed that fan blades had been installed incorrectly; days after they had accomplished a fan blade lube check on the #1 engine of a B737-700. Engine vibration troubleshooting led to the cause of the discrepancy.
An FA2000 encountered a B757 wake vortex at about 9000 ft on the LAX RIIVR to Runway 25L. The reporter was using a HUD to remain above the traffic.

Pilot taking a Commercial flight test retracted and collapsed the landing gear on a touch-and-go roll rather than retracting the flaps.
Lear 60 loses 600 feet in turbulence encounter at FL410.

B757 made an emergency descent and landed at the nearest suitable airport when unable to maintain cabin pressurization.

B737 on visual approach to LAS fails to remain above Class B floor because of early descent.

CRJ200 Captain is concerned when maintenance asks him to enter corrective actions in the logbook following the successful completion of a QRC procedure in response to an engine bleed malfunction.
B757-200 flight crew reports inability to retract landing gear after takeoff. Landing gear handle will not move past the off position. A safe return to field ensues.
A319 diverted to a nearby airport for a maintenance inspection of a fluctuating oil quantity indicator.
SF340 flight crew reports generator failure descending out of FL230. Checklist is complied with and an emergency is declared; followed by an uneventful landing at destination.
An SF340 flight crew experienced right-hand AC Generator caution light and after conferring with dispatch elected to return to their departure airport.
Sail plane pilot misjudges thermal activity for the day and flies beyond the point of safe return to the departure airport. An off airport landing ensues.

Both flight test pilots aboard a B777 undergoing a post maintenance flight check reacted unilaterally to an over temperature of the right engine following a shutdown and re-light test. Result was both engine fuel shut off levers being actuated. Quick reaction to restore the left engine minimized the consequences.
C172 in right traffic for Runway 22 at CDW experienced NMAC at 1200 FT with departure from Runway 28.
A GII encountered a B757's wake at 1300 ft after departing SNA and involuntarily descended to 900 ft.

text: A DHC-8 flight crew encountered a pressurization problem followed by the failure of the First Officer's windshield. They diverted to the nearest suitable airport.
A M20K pilot experienced a rough running engine on a cross country flight. He declared an emergency and diverted to the nearest airport; where he found water in the right fuel tank.

Freighter Captain lands at Bethel and announces braking action fair on CTAF. Airport worker announces shortly that braking action is nil and the airport is closed. Aircraft on final announces they will be landing then reports braking action as fair to good. Airport worker did not want aircraft to pack snow that he would be removing from runway.
A Captain of an A320 raises concerns about his carrier abusing the MEL procedures and not repairing their aircraft; when maintenance and parts were available.
PA28 pilot is very confused by new ramp construction and diagram provided by FBO. Reporter is unable to locate taxiway C and ends up on D headed Northeast.
A B737 flight crew reported taking off with incorrect zero fuel weight figure that resulted in takeoff weight almost 2000 LBS higher than planned.
Deadheading pilot reports Cabin Attendant announcing the presence of an FFDO on the flight over the public address system before passengers boarded; but while cleaners were still on board.

A DHC-8 flight crew got a red gear unsafe light and warning horn after extending the landing gear. They declared an emergency; followed procedures; determined the gear was down; had equipment standing by; and made a normal landing.
An A319 flight crew received a 'TERRAIN TERRAIN PULL UP' warning on a night visual approach to ABQ Runway 26. They leveled until warning stopped and then continued approach to a safe landing.
EMB145 flight crew report 'BAGG SMOKE' EICAS message during taxi. After firing the bottle and calling CFR it is determined that the warning is false.

text: B757-200 flight crew reports high oil temperature passing 15;000 FT on climb out and returns to departure airport after declaring an emergency.
C402 pilot reports insidious electrical failure that nearly results in a gear up landing but does result in propeller damage during go-around.
PA30 pilot reports landing with left brake locked causing a runway excursion. No apparent damage or injuries occur.

B757 First Officer reports flap overspeed departing SLLP. When an attempt is made to revise the route of flight to W11 to remain below FL200; the FMC will not accept the route. A discrepancy is noted between the departure chart; which shows W11 passing over CAL VOR and the airway chart which does not use the CAL VOR.
BE76 Instructor pilot reports assuming control from student during landing attempt when student begins drifting left prior to touchdown. During go-around right wing tip contacts runway.

PA-28 student pilot practicing touch-and-goes in the pattern encountered wake turbulence from the preceding C172.

A Mechanic reports a B767-300 returned to the gate; right after pushback; #2 engine did not have an IDG indication.
A B777-200 equipped with Rolls Royce engines developed a fuel leak in a line between the tank and the engine after a foam liner between a bracket and fuel line wore away.

Widebody Captain reports taxiway excursion in freezing conditions during taxi to the ramp after landing at CYMX. The crew is advised after the fact that Taxiway J would have been a better choice due to it being recently sanded. CYMX is uncontrolled.
Two B757 Flight Attendants report the sights and sounds of an engine failure shortly after takeoff; with return to departure airport.

Mechanic reports he missed noticing damage to one of the elevator assemblies on a B737-300; during a Detailed Visual Inspection. Damage was caused by the potable water servicing door panel previously departing the aircraft.
B757 First Officer reports auto cabin pressurization failure in two stages starting at FL390. Flight is able to continue to destination with manual pressurization.
AZO Controller described conflict event at 7000 FT when they failed to accurately judge climb performance coupled with other distracting position duties.

G450 flight crew is cleared and briefed the BANYO4 departing SDL. Once airborne on the 300 degree heading Controller issues 290 degree heading to intercept PXR 321 degree radial. The crew does not comprehend that this radial is different from the SID radial causing an early turn and a track deviation.

text: A B757-200 Captain experienced an engine flameout after start during push back.
A320 flight crew at FL370 experienced light mountain wave which turned into severe turbulence and resulted in an overspeed situation.

An air carrier flight crew member described difficulty donning his oxygen mask while wearing the headset and recommended that flight crews practice the procedure to avoid potential problems during high altitude decompressions.

Q400 flight crew at a Canadian outstation noticed a 12 inch cut in the tread of a main tire. Contract maintenance initially states the tire must be replaced; after conferring with company maintenance the decision is reversed to the flight crew's dismay.

An A319 flight crew experienced ECAM message #1 IDG LO OIL PRESS. They ran the procedure and returned to land at departure airport. After Maintenance action they took off and experienced the same problem once again. They again returned to land.

Cold soaked CRJ-900 utilizing external power and an air cart received 'R PACK HI TEMP' and 'SMOKE TOILET' caution messages while parked at the gate. Smoke was in the cabin; but there was no checklist for the 'caution' message; only a 'warning.'

A C172 pilot lost control during landing and experienced a runway excursion.

An Avionics Mechanic reports on the difficulty reading the wire identification markings in the forward cargo pit ceiling of a B777-200. A hydraulic pump wire bundle had overheated; shorted and arced and damaged the cabin floor beam.
ARTCC Controller described engine out emergency incident; the aircraft landing several feet short of the runway.
A B767-400 flight crew holding short of Taxiway G on H4 at MCO was forced to announce on Ground Control frequency that an oncoming Airbus taxiing on G must stop to avoid a collision.

B737NG flight crew report compressor stalls and engine failure at FL400 with diversion to nearest suitable airport. Uneventful landing ensues after rejecting company request to return to departure airport.
Air carrier flight crew on approach to BUR; experienced a NMAC with general aviation aircraft in the pattern at VNY.
A B737 crew exited PHX Runway 8 and taxied onto Taxiway 'T' when the taxi clearance was Taxiway 'S'. The signage at 'S' and 'T' was not clear enough to direct the crew onto 'S.'

A319 First Officer windscreen seal failed at FL370; fight crew requested lower and after failed radio communications with Dispatch and Maintenance decided a divert was their best situation. Emergency was declared followed by an uneventful landing.
DHC-8-100 flight crew on departure notice their tail de-ice boot is inoperative; a return to the departure airport ensued.
A B777's center fuel tank pump would not shut down; even below 2400 pounds. The circuit breakers were pulled at 300 pounds.
Citabria 8KCAB pilot had a prop strike after losing control of the aircraft while taxiing in a gusty quartering tailwind situation.

DC-9 on SOLDO RNAV SID from DFW; experienced a course deviation when two waypoints dropped out of the FMS unnoticed by them.

Cessna 425 pilot experiences a NMAC with training helicopters in the uncontrolled traffic pattern at F45.

A B767 Captain called off a trip fatigued because the trip bidding software did not take into account circadian rhythm when transitioning from one bid month's last trip to the next month's first trip.
A C182 encountered wake turbulence at 350 FT on final approach at VNY. The preceding aircraft was a small jet. Wind conditions were reported calm.

An SF340 Captain had to brake abruptly to avoid an encounter with a potable water truck.
Air carrier taxiing for departure from DFW failed to comply with assigned taxi instructions causing a minor conflict with another aircraft.
Air carrier flight crew allows Cabin Attendant to occupy the cockpit jump seat on a flight for which all the cabin seats were occupied.

An MD80 altitude select knob was unknowingly changed to a lower altitude which then armed automatically without any pilot input. The altitude set knob turned with minimum input force leading to an altitude deviation.

Both flight test pilots aboard a B777 undergoing a post maintenance flight check reacted unilaterally to an over temperature of the right engine following a shutdown and re-light test. Result was both engine fuel shut off levers being actuated. Quick reaction to restore the left engine minimized the consequences.
A B737 Mechanic and Captain report placement of a security seal on a lavatory oxygen mask door; which will render the emergency oxygen system in the lavatory inoperative.

A Lead Mechanic describes his involvement with securing an APU inlet door in the closed position; due to an APU that would not start on a CRJ aircraft. Safety wire failed in landing and the APU door opened; allowing the APU to windmill; requiring replacement.
After suffering a significant engine vibration the pilot of a PA28 elected to proceed to other than the nearest suitable airport due to minimal assets at the nearest.
A light transport jet crew failed to see a NOTAM for the APF ZEILR2 arrival requiring a 150 degree heading after ZEILR.
Evidence of a possible leak in the left main tank of a B777 caused the flight crew to divert to a nearby oceanic airport for maintenance examination.

A Mechanic with an Inspection Authority (IA) rating; reports on his involvement with repairs and maintenance on a Lycoming IO360 in a Cessna Cardinal that required an emergency landing. Owner/Operator also performed maintenance on the engine; but was not licensed.
While descending to meet a crossing restriction; a Gulfstream 200 received and responded to a TCAS TA and RA with an unspecified model Airbus.
C310 pilot is notified by ATC that he is more than 3;000 FT below the altitude indicated on the primary altimeter. Standby altimeter verifies the error.
B737NG flight crew misinterpret PDC route.

A CRJ900 Captain reported falling into microsleep on approach as a result of extreme fatigue due to scheduling practices at his airline.
B737 First Officer reports altitude deviation during the DELTA2 RNAV arrival to SLC.
An LJ55 flight crew experienced low fuel level light on descent. They declared an emergency and their arrival was expedited.
A non GPS B737-400's flight guidance did not track an RNAV departure correctly and caused a track deviation.

DA50 Captain reports altitude deviation on the TEB 5 departure; climbing to 2000 FT prior to the TEB 4.5 DME.

A B767-200 flight crew encountered a REV (engine reverser not stowed) warning. Visual inspection seemed to indicate partial deployment so they declared an emergency and diverted to the nearest suitable airport.
B777 Flight Attendant reports discovering during boarding that FAMs may be aboard but unannounced to the crew.
Air Carrier pilot voiced concern regarding ATC routing assignments with regard to direct airport vs. VOR; when identifications are the same.
A C208 pilot lost control of his aircraft when he experienced severe turbulence and icing enroute to his destination. He cited fatigue issues as contributing to the severity of the incident.
An SR22 pilot encountered unforecast icing conditions; declared an emergency; and diverted to an enroute airport.
A CRJ700 flight crew experienced a PROX SYSTEM FAIL message after takeoff. They declared an emergency; ran the procedure; and returned to land at their departure airport.
A CRJ900 flight crew experienced caution message DC EMER BUS after takeoff. They ran the procedure and returned to land overweight at their departure airport.

A B767-300 flight crew experienced EICAS message 'LE FLAP AYMMETRICAL.' They ran the procedure; coordinated with Dispatch and Maintenance; and returned to departure airport for a flaps 20 approach and landing.
Air carriers landing PHL; Runway 27R with traffic landing Runway 35; described minimal separation event; Reporter questioned ATC spacing judgment.
Air carrier landing Runway 27R at PHL described minimal separation event with traffic landing Runway 35; go-around issued to Runway 35 traffic; Reporter questioned ATC spacing judgment.

CRJ flight crew rushed on an early morning departure received an aircraft with hydraulic pump 1B deferred. The flight departed normally and has various other alerts in-flight; upon arrival it is noticed that there is in fact a burst hydraulic line not an inoperative pump as the deferral stated.
CRJ-200 flight crew on departure received a left engine oil pressure warning; they ran the appropriate procedure and determined it was prudent to return to their departure airport.
Turboprop on departure from DTW experienced multiple bird strikes climbing through 1800 FT MSL; they successfully returned to the field.
B757 flight crew encountered multiple system malfunctions shortly after takeoff. Believed anomalies to have been the result of a failed electrical bus.
A B737-500'S flaps 1 and slats remained extended after takeoff with the flap handle up. The aircraft was returned to land but an emergency was not declared.
Air carrier landing ORD being vectored at 5000 FT for Runway 9R experienced conflict with traffic on parallel Runway 10; ATC admitted operational error.
A319 Captain describes the procedural and clearance deviations that he suffered before declaring fatigue and removing himself from the pairing.

Hawker 800 flight crew rejects takeoff due to no airspeed indication on Captains side. Pitot cover is found to be installed with no flag. Pitot cover and static port pins are normally connected together and have a single large flag. The fact that they had become separated was over looked on preflight.
C172 student pilot loses control of the aircraft after landing; damaging a runway edge light.
On landing a private aircraft on a private unimproved field; pilot lost control and had a prop strike.

A B757 fuel crossfeed valve malfunction permitted the right fuel tank pumps to feed both engines after the crossfeed valve was closed because center tank fuel usage was ceased. A fuel imbalance resulted. An emergency diversion was made to nearby airport.

A B737-700 crew reported that their aircraft was released with an open MEL. The MEL paperwork was not referenced on the flight release and because the MEL item was common to this air carrier's mixed B737 fleet type the B737-770 aircraft requirement was different from earlier aircraft models.

B737-500 flight crewmember addressed poor scheduling practices for reserve pilots. Felt that allowing the schedulers to 'reset' reserves' rest period in the middle of a previously 'set' rest period results in the inability to obtain adequate rest prior to the 'now legal' later assignment.
Dispatchers report concerning SF340 crew decision to return after detecting high turbine temperature during climb out.
B777 Captain reports evasive action to avoid geese at 500 FT AGL during approach to ORD.

A B737-400's main landing gear green lights failed to illuminate with the gear handle down. While performing the 'Gear Lights Disagree' checklist the 'AIR/GND RELAY & LTS' circuit breaker's extension was missed. A normal landing followed resetting the CIRCUIT BREAKER.
MD88 Captain learns after the fact that the 250 KT restrictions for southern departures on the ORD3 is still in effect.

Local Controller described conflict with 2 successive departures; requiring the use of visual separation; claiming fatigue as a causal factor of the incident.

An MD83 flight crew experienced TAIL COMP TEMP HIGH warning. They declared an emergency and returned to departure airport for an overweight landing.
An A320 flight crew experienced ECAM warning HYD Y RSVR LO LVL. They ran the procedure; coordinated with dispatch and maintenance; declared an emergency; and continued to destination.
A319 flight crew experienced degraded steering after landing due to the failure of the scissor link pin.
A B737 Captain inadvertently shut down both engines taxiing to gate.
Dash 8-300 flight crew exits runway on taxiway with paint crew at work at left edge. No NOTAM was issued nor did ATIS close this taxiway. After taxi in latest ATIS did close this taxiway.
E190 Captain reports the autopilot deviated substantially from the localizer after capture.

text: B737 Captain expresses concern over manager attempts to intimidate him in response to his refusal to accept an aircraft with an inoperative APU.
An A320 pilot comments that CRT readability is greatly decreased during bright ambient light conditions. The air carrier maintenance did not replace the unreadable CRT.
A CE-680 Captain reports an electrical smell in the flight station at about the time the MCDU failed. The crew declared an emergency and diverted to a nearby airport. No smoke or flames developed.

text: CE680 flight crew reports a slightly late turn to 280 degrees during the TEB5 Departure due to a slow climb and questioning the turn timing.
