text: A CRJ-700's main cabin door struck a ramp worker as it was being opened after arrival. The worker was retrieving wheel chocks which were left on the ramp in a location near where a parked CRJ-200's wheels would be located.

A CL-60's landing gear handle would not go to the full down position before landing so the EMERGENCY GEAR EXTENSION checklist was used prior to an emergency landing. A bolt and nut from a previous windshield change were found to be obstructing the handle.
EMB190 Captain reports compressor stall below 80 KTS during takeoff attempt and reject.

B757 Captain reports APU fault light after second engine start at gate; and agrees to continue flight with deferral and repairs at next stop. Reporter is contacted by duty manager as to reason for refusal at next stop.
A319 flight crew report yellow hydraulic system failure at FL360. After conferring with maintenance crew elects to continue to destination for uneventful landing.
CRJ-200 Captain and First Officer report the left engine thrust lever jammed at full thrust 95% during climb. An emergency was declared and the crew executed a single engine landing.

A319 Captain reports BCL1 fault during climb out. After reviewing aircraft maintenance history and consulting maintenance; crew elects to divert for repairs. Battery 1 is turned off for the remainder of the flight and BCL1 is changed after landing.

A Mechanic working one of two trucks involved with deicing a B737-800; reports on communication problems with the Flight Crew and improving procedures to prevent deicing fluid being drawn into the air conditioning systems.
CE560 Captain reports encountering severe turbulence during climb after penetrating a building cell not painted on radar.
show: 2009-02 · Inflight: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Cruise

text: CE560 First Officer reports reaching 1700 ft on the TEB5 before correcting back to 1500 ft as required by the procedure.

A small aircraft pilot descended below the MDA for Petaluma airport's VOR approach shortly after sunset. A near CFIT event occurred but a nearby tree line provided a visual cue that made him climb back to the VASI.
Pilot of tail wheel aircraft reports flipping nose over when overly aggressive braking is used prior to firm contact with the runway.
show: 2009-03 · Ground: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Landing

text: PA28 glider tow pilot reports airborne conflict with B737 after releasing glider at 3000 ft 25 NM west of EWR.
A fatigued B747 crew began an early descent to their destination in VFR conditions after believing the aircraft was high on glide path.
CL65 Captain reports unstabilized approach and landing. The poor performance is attributed to fatigue caused by 4 days of flying with the last day experiencing many delays due to weather.
ZMA Controller described loss of separation and airspace incursion event when an air carrier accepted frequency change and ATC descent instructions for a company aircraft.

L30 Controller receiving OJT experienced operational error when aircraft being vectored for a visual approach entered a MVA area below the appropriate altitude; reporter claiming facility visual turn on procedure was contributory.
show: 2009-03 · ATC Issue All Types · Initial Approach

text: A300 flight crew reports green hydraulic system failure at top of descent. ECAM procedures are complied with and an emergency is declared. After landing aircraft is towed to gate.
A pilot reports crossing VGT Runway 7 at Taxiway G because he did not recognize the taxiway as an intersection with the runway. The blue plywood sign on Taxiway G was non standard.
Flight instructor asks student to check NOTAMS and discovers after the fact that landings were practiced at a closed airport.
PCT Controller described event allegedly involving ZDC Controllers assigning arrival procedure that is NOTAMed not authorized.
show: 2009-03 · Procedural: Published Material / Policy · Initial Approach

text: A320 Captain reports finding all 4 engine fire squib circuit breakers pulled during preflight; apparently by maintenance several days earlier during an engine change. Aircraft had apparently been operated on revenue flights in this condition.
EMB170 Captain reports learning after the fact that his aircraft has been serviced with the incorrect type of hydraulic fluid and was grounded.

B737NG is dispatched on MEL 29-10; A side engine driven pump cannot be deactivated. First officer misunderstands and starts number one engine during push back causing tow bar to break. Flight departs after replacement tow bar is found.
A B737-300 encounters wake from a B737-800; requests deviation from track to escape the turbulence but in the confusion the crew does not raise the flaps before flap speed limit is exceeded.
Several rows of passenger oxygen masks dropped when the First Officer's umbrella accidentally momentarily activated a B717 passenger Oxygen Mask Eject switch then left it in a normal position.
An ERJ-170 flight crew experienced several hot starts complicated by power interruptions that hid the EGT gauges momentarily.
Air carrier described approach event when ATC's instructions were lengthy; complex and difficult to comply with because of aircraft characteristics.
show: 2009-03 · Procedural: Published Material / Policy · Initial Approach

text: B737 flight crew departing PSP realizes airborne they are not familiar with the new CATH9 departure procedure and turn the wrong way at PSP VOR.
show: 2009-03 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Climb

text: B757-200 flight crew experienced a complete loss of hydraulic fluid in the left system. PTU backup failed as well due to complete loss of fluid in the reservoir. Landed safely using manual procedures for gear and flaps.

A319 First Officer expressed concern over flight crew schedules which switch between all-nighters and day time operations. Feels they are unquestionably upsetting to the diurnal cycle of pilots who experience such scheduling.

Large transport flight crew report bird strike departing CLT. After noting change in engine pitch and sight increase in vibration; crew elects to return. Evidence of bird strike is found on post flight.

An ATC Local Controller reported to a departing aircraft that its right engine was producing black smoke. The crew returned to land and was told by the runway safety crew that smoke and leaking fluid was coming from the engine. Maintenance found a fuel leak.
show: 2009-03 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Takeoff
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: A300 flight crew reports electrical malfunction during landing causing anti skid to fail and all eight main gear tires to blow. Aircraft had been dispatched with one generator inoperative and the APU running. APU apparently failed during landing roll.
show: 2009-03 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Landing
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: A319 Captain reports discovering on preflight that broken ENG Master Switch spring had been deferred under MEL for ENG MAN Control Switch. These switches are completely different and the ENG Master is not deferrable.
B757-200; on a left base and cleared for a visual approach to Runway 6 at BDL received a low altitude alert from the Approach Controller.

PCT Controller described an alleged pilot deviation reference an early descent on the ELDEE 4 STAR; claiming Supervisor failed to process pilot deviation; adding; several aircraft have failed to meet the restrictions on this STAR.
show: 2009-02 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Descent

text: Following lengthy ground delays in blowing snow the A319 flight crew returned to the gate to be de-iced a second time. Visual inspection of the wing leading edge discovered ice the length of both wings despite a time interval of less than the calculated holdover time.
PCT TRACON Controller believed ATC was inappropriately clearing flights via the WZRRD STAR to DCA notwithstanding the arrival was notamed 'out.'
A320 flight crew reports missing crossing restriction during arrival. Fatigue and one pilot talking on company radio are cited as factors.
show: 2009-03 · Flight Deck: Illness / Injury · Initial Approach

text: A320 Captain reported arrival gate closure at DEN has lead to ATC utilizing various delay mechanisms. The change is not posted in NOTAMS; Reporter suggested for planning purposes; specifically fuel; it be included.

With the engines at idle in the flare; the flight crew of a CRJ100 is forced to reject the landing due to gusty crosswinds which displaced the aircraft from the runway centerline.  When the engine and aircraft acceleration response proved to be marginal; a stick shaker resulted.  Reporter suggested the use of maximum thrust be made SOP for such situations.

COS TRACON Controller described unauthorized entry into adjacent airspace; claiming stored data information on the military flight as well as handoff symbology caused an assumption that a handoff had been accomplished.
DA50 flight crew initiates climb without a clearance.
show: 2009-03 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Cruise

text: Relief pilot of a B767 felt that fuel should have been jetisonned prior to landing when they returned above maximum landing weight to the departure airport due to a passenger illness.
Inexperienced student pilot of a C182 RG cites shifting winds as a contributing factor to a runway excursion following landing.
S56 Controller described proximity event when Final Controller failed to ensure final turn on to an aircraft on a visual approach resulting in a near loss of separation.

Beechcraft A36 pilot on final for one runway experienced a NMAC with a Beechcraft Skipper flown by an apparently disoriented pilot who flew his base leg across the extended runway centerline for the parallel runway.
Pilot of P180 fails to note NOTAM revising ZEILR STAR to APF.
BE33 suffers gear collapse upon landing.
show: 2009-03 · Ground: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Landing

text: ZID Associate Controller described operational error event when Mode C altitude swap occurred and Controller providing OJT failed to note developing situation; corrective action issued was too late to maintain separation.

AUS Controller providing OJT chronicled a near loss of separation event when two aircraft being handed off; involving two sectors; and in the process of changing frequencies required immediate turns to avoid a conflict.
A320 flight crew experienced a power supply interruption due to an arcing and burned connector which resulted in multiple ECAM messages and irregular procedure reference actions.
Cleared via the CATHEDRAL NINE departure at PSP; flight crew of an MD80 failed to fly the procedure track to EMRUD and back to PSP.
show: 2009-03 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Climb

text: PDX TRACON Controller described NMAC event; primary radar traffic was issued; inbound air carrier executed evasive action; reporter suggesting establishment of Class B to prevent additional occurrences.
Inexperienced Cessna 172 pilot encountered unintended flight into IMC and suffered spatial disorientation. ATC provides an assist.
A Captain reports he noticed the Yaw Dampers would not engage properly when he was flying a CRJ-900. The Yaw Damper switches were found to be installed in reverse order (backwards).
A321 flight crew aborted takeoff at low speed due to right engine failure.
When the left IRS failed the flight crew of a B737NG was surprised the QRC did not direct them to select the right IRS. Encountered several failure mode indications during remainder of the flight.
CRJ200 returned to departure airport after receiving a flaps fail message on climb out.

A DHC-8-400 pilot describes the passenger comfort issues; the difficulty operating the aircraft with manual pressurization and the resulting safety degradation when the pilot monitoring is totally engrossed operating the pressurization.
Q400 First Officer questions the terminology of the approach controller who clears him for an 'ILS Approach; Glide Slope out of service' instead of a 'Localizer Approach.'
show: 2009-03 · Procedural: Published Material / Policy · Initial Approach

text: Air carrier descending into DCA on the ELDEE 4 STAR missed crossing restriction; Controller reports numerous similar events.
show: 2009-03 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Descent

text: Failure to turn on pitot heat results in a possible altimetry error on the part of a PA32 private pilot.
A single piloted aircraft was issued a BLUBELL2 ARRIVAL direct to COWZZ intersection arriving at TME. The Reporter discovered that his GPS did not include the BLUBELL2 because it did not serve TME.

A CRJ crew executed a go-around at 30' after gusty winds pushed the aircraft to the runway's side. Because the aircraft's right engine did not accelerate immediately; the aircraft slowed and the stall warning activated. The task saturated crew failed to notify ATC of the go around.

A small aircraft pilot did not recognize the assigned taxiway A7 before incurring HIO Runway 2/20. The pilot was using a current AF/D airport chart which is not updated to reflect the current A6/A7 designations changes.

A B737-NG experienced a dual FMC reset on the ATL CANUK 7 RNAV arrival because of a route discontinuity that was not obvious to the flight crew. All FMC and ND indications were normal up to the point of the reset.
show: 2009-03 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Initial Approach

text: A SR-20 Instructor pilot reported that his student executed a go-around after a porpoised landing caused by wind shift on final. During the go around a LAHSO clearance was unavoidably not adhered too.
show: 2009-03 · Ground: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Landing

text: PHL TRACON Controller voiced concern regarding Tower issued clearance; non compliant with established procedures; adding the facility's failure to provide a good method of addressing same type issues.

An HS-125-700 developed an intermittent vibration of unknown origin at cruise. During descent; the right engine developed a vibration and was shutdown. An emergency was declared and the aircraft continued to its destination.

An A320; with a history electrical problem; departed after maintenance assures the crew the aircraft was fixed. During descent at the destination a momentary AC BUS2 ECAM alerted followed by electrical and electronic equipment disconnecting.
IFR PA-34 at 8000 FT; with P31; encountered weather buildups; requested and was granted an amended route; after hand off to VPS reporter was questioned regarding restricted airspace entry.
A321 broke the tow bar and damaged the nose gear when the Captain inadvertently set the brakes while the aircraft was still being pushed back.
B737 flight crew reports track deviation departing SLC for ZZZ due to errors connecting the WEVIC1 KSINO departure with the STAR for the relatively close destination airport.
show: 2009-03 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Climb

text: CE680 flight crew experience jammed stabilizer on departure and after consulting emergency checklist; return for uneventful flaps 15 landing.
A319 flight crew report yellow hydraulic system failure at FL390. After conferring with maintenance crew elects to continue to destination for uneventful landing.
show: 2009-03 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Cruise
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: B737-300 flight crew report aircraft making 'S' turns with autopilot and LNAV engaged on the HAROB3 SID from Runway 16C at SEA. RNP is noted at 2.8 during this event. Once RNP begins to return to normal LNAV also returns to normal.
show: 2009-03 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Initial Climb

text: Cleared to cross an intersection at 17000 FT MSL; flight crew of B737NG failed to set altitude in MCP altitude window and thus did not begin descent in a timely fashion. Reporter cites inconsistent VNAV SOP and lack of familiarity with programming the FMC.
P180 flight crew reports runway excursion after landing in strong crosswind conditions.
Beechcraft King Air suffered the loss of an engine cowling inspection door in flight which then struck the tail.
C172 pilot reports propeller and engine failure with extreme vibration just after lift off. Aircraft is successfully landed in the runway remaining.
A B767-300 received a 'LE FLAP ASYM' message while selecting flaps 20 degrees on approach. The QRH procedures were completed on the missed approach followed by a normal landing.
MD80 First Officer reports an altitude deviation he believed to have been caused by his inadvertent change of the altitude alert setting when he tuned the VOR.
ZJX Controller described operational deviation when distractions and lack of RADAR Associate Controller contributed to an unauthorized airspace entry.

VFR RV-6 with M98 TRACON for traffic advisories; maintaining clearance from Class B; assumed ATC coordinated transition of STP Class B when in fact ATC expected the reporter to obtain the subject clearance.
show: 2009-03 · Airspace Violation All Types · Initial Approach

text: Private pilot attempts to exit runway too quickly and suffers an excursion.
An SR20 pilot experienced a rough running engine shortly after takeoff. The pilot returned to takeoff airport and found the right magneto had failed.
Robinson R22 pilot inadvertently took off with ground handling wheels still installed. One fell off while airborne.
PCT Controller described airspace entry event; indicating no NOTAM or other process have been initiated to notify the user community.
show: 2009-03 · Airspace Violation All Types · Initial Approach

text: ZJX Controller experienced an operational error at FL350 when issuing a climb clearance to one aircraft; failing to note the filed route of a conflicting aircraft; resulting in a head on conflict; corrective action was too late to secure separation.
Instrument rated private pilot feels he may have taken off with carburetor ice.

Tower Controller described event when a B747 departure had crossed the runway hold line; experienced some problem and declined takeoff; CRJ traffic on base was advised of the situation and given a landing clearance.

Cessna 172 crossed the active runway hold short line at night while cleared to follow another aircraft taxiing to the same runway. The Cessna pilot was unaware the aircraft they were following had been cleared for an intersection departure rather than the full length.

NMAC is reported between a Waco on go-around and a C310 making low pass with landing gear issues. The reporter (Waco) had coordinated with the C310 pilot but botched the landing and needed to go-around.
show: 2009-03 · Inflight: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Landing

text: A CRJ-700 flight crew received 'GEAR DISAGREE' warning message in cruise flight. They ran the procedure; declared an emergency; and diverted to the nearest suitable airport.

Light twin on downwind for Runway 17L at COS with instructor and student have NMAC with student pilot departing Runway 12 heading 080 degrees as instructed by Tower. Call from Tower for student pilot to level at 6500 FT is late and goes unheard. Controller training was apparently also taking place.
Air carrier flight crew misunderstood amended PDC and enters wrong route in FMC. ATC notices the track error and sets them straight.
show: 2009-03 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Cruise

text: A CRJ-700 developed a strong odor accompanied by the SMOKE AFT LAV Master Caution Warning after takeoff. An emergency return to land was completed. The crew was told that an engine wash the previous night that may have left a chemical residue in the engines.

cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: ZOA Controller experienced operational error at FL370 during non radar oceanic procedures when failing to note an aircraft position report had inadvertently been deleted.

An air carrier Captain in a reserve status describes a scheduling 'reset' in which a call at the beginning of his scheduled duty period will 'reset' (continue) rest so that he can be scheduled to fly later in the day. The reset interferes with rest planning and can create a very long day with an interrupted rest prior to reporting for duty.
A B737 crew experienced a normal landing after being informed during descent that a tire may had shredded on the previous takeoff. Tire damaged was found after landing.
A B747-400 flight crew reported that a NOTAM affecting reporting procedures on their international flight is often omitted from their paperwork.

A DHC8-400 (Q-400) aft cabin door did not completely close before takeoff causing a FUSELAGE DOORS warning in flight. After a return to land the crew was told this was the fourth aft cabin door event for this same aircraft.

B737 Captain reports applying the MEL procedure for a failed left ignition while the right ignition had actually failed. The MEL requires an operating ignition be connected to the AC standby bus for dispatch.
Cessna 680 flight crew opted not to fly the obstacle departure clearance out of MMH as cleared in their IFR flight plan.
show: 2009-03 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Initial Climb

text: B777-200 flight crew experienced an EGPWS terrain warning at 500 FT AGL on and ILS approach in VMC conditions to Runway 19R at IAD.

A Flight Attendant reported significant deviations from procedure when boarding FAMs; resulting in potential identity and location information. The Reporter recommended that boarding agents not bear responsibility for FAM paperwork.
Flight crew experienced a TAWS warning on approach to Runway 13 at DVL after briefing to be aware of a possible warning. They missed the approach and returned to departure airport.

B747-400 Captain refused the aircraft assigned to his flight because of long term deferral of landing gear retraction mechanism requiring the routine use of an irregular procedure to retract the landing gear.
A Citation crew completed a BVS Runway 10 RNAV straight in approach deleting the procedure turn. ATC stated that a procedure turn should have been completed.
show: 2009-03 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Initial Approach

text: B757 flight crew report TCAS RA at 10300 FT approaching SSCOT intersection on the SSCOT1 RNAV to MIA. Controller work load is cited as possible contributing factor.

During taxi in after landing the tail of a Cessna 208 Caravan settled to the ground due to an excessively aft CG. Pilot is openly critical of the company load planners and the processes they use to provide data to pilots.
show: 2009-03 · Ground: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Taxi

text: A Bell 222 pilot reported losing part of his engine cowl; most likely from a bird strike.
After takeoff Bombardier Dash 8 First Officer is unable to raise the nose gear. Post flight inspection reveals that the nose gear locking pin is engaged.
A B737-300 flight crew reported losing pressurization. They ran the procedure; declared an emergency; and descended to a safe altitude while they diverted to the nearest suitable airport.

A Q400 flight crew experienced master caution 'ROLL SPLR OUTBD GND' message just before takeoff. They were operating under an MEL affecting the spoilers; but their procedure would not allow a takeoff with this message displayed.
A CRJ700 flight crew reported low oil pressure and high oil temperature on climb out. They ran engine shutdown procedures and returned to their departure airport.
A B777-200 flight crew on an international over water flight experienced a generator drive failure. They followed procedure; disconnected the drive; started the APU; and continued to destination.
Non-EFIS; non-GPS equipped B737 suffered a track deviation on an RNAV SID. Appears to have been the result of a route discontinuity that was not observed during the preflight route verification.
show: 2009-01 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Takeoff

text: PA28 suffers significant damage when the nose gear collapses and the aircraft exits the runway.
A C210 pilot on an IFR flight plan encountered icing conditions and climbed from his assigned altitude without a clearance.
Pilot of Lancair 4 PT may have violated Class C airspace when he experienced full scale uncommanded yaw damper deflections shortly after takeoff.
A300 Captain rejects takeoff when auto throttles are engaged prior to engines being spooled and aircraft being aligned with runway. Aircraft on approach is instructed to go around.

GV Captain reports missing crossing restriction at DANDY during ILS 6 at TEB. Speed was maintained until late in the approach and the clearance was to circle to land Runway 1; which added complexity to the procedure.
show: 2009-03 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Initial Approach

text: B737 Captain on visual approach to Runway 1 at DCA reports conflict with Dash on visual to Runway 33. Dash crew commences approach abeam B737 and never slows; resulting in Tower issuing a go-around to the Dash crew.
B737 First Officer discovers kneepads in engine inlet during heavy rain; apparently placed there by Ramper hoping to keep them dry. Pads are removed.

PA28 pilot experiences total electrical failure during IFR flight in IMC. Reporter makes best attempt at remaining on flight plan and lands at destination airport. Post flight reveals alternator drive belt had failed.
show: 2009-03 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Cruise

text: CL601 flight crew report FMS failure during arrival to SLC. Crew requests vectors from ATC and uneventful approach and landing ensues.
show: 2009-03 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Initial Approach

text: E145 FMS on the KENNEDY ONE SID; CANARSIE climb attempted to proceed from the CRI 176/2 crossing restriction fix directly to COATE intersection vice flying the 176 radial for vectors per the SID.
show: 2009-03 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Climb

text: A Q400 flight crew experienced landing gear unsafe lights on final approach. They coordinated with Dispatch and Maintenance; ran the alternate landing gear extend procedure; and landed normally.
Air carrier flight crew; on the ROKIT STAR into HOU; experience a course deviation when they fail to follow the published transition.
show: 2009-03 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Initial Approach

text: A B737-300 flight crew was dispatched with a generator inoperative and the APU substituting. After takeoff the APU failed so the flight crew returned to land at their departure airport.
A CRJ200 flight crew reported experiencing an APU fire on taxi in when they made a third start attempt contrary to limitations.

text: Track deviation and low altitude alert in mountainous terrain followed the clearance to fly a published missed approach that had not been briefed in advance by the Cessna 750 flight crew.

MCI Controller experienced operational error at 3000 FT with two aircraft on final. Wake separation was compromised when second aircraft was slow to respond to the reporters corrective break out action.
show: 2009-03 · ATC Issue All Types · Initial Approach

text: A light plane pilot reported a minor collision with a parked aircraft even though he was on the taxiway centerline. Apparently a local maintenance facility uses an overflow parking area that was a factor in the collision.
Experimental Long-EZ pilot executed an off airport landing after running a fuel tank dry and an unsuccessful attempt at switching fuel tanks.

MD10 Captain reports manifold #2 fail alert passing 15000 FT in climb. Thrust is reduced to idle in accordance with procedures; fuel is dumped and uneventful landing ensues. Post-flight reveals faulty sensor.
A80 Controller voiced concern regarding frequent instances of one air carrier's aircraft flying through the localizer during simultaneous approach procedures.
show: 2009-03 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Initial Approach

text: SMA pilot reported exposed runway end lights at convergence of departure ends of Runways 14 and 5 at VVS are a taxi hazard.

text: B757-200 experienced alarming bumps in flight which were the result of ice forming around the potable water service door due to the servicing valve either malfunctioning or a failure of the ground crew to properly secure it after servicing.
B737NG flight crew abandoned a CAT 3 ILS approach when they belatedly became aware the procedure is NOTAM'd out of service.

Approaching FL180 EMB145 flight crew detects electrical fumes and declares an emergency. After complying with flight manual procedures; fumes began to dissipate and crew elects to return to departure airport.
show: 2009-03 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Climb
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: Air carrier crew continues down Taxiway K rather than turning onto Taxiway T12 to hold short of Runway 32L at ORD.

BE58 pilot reports engine failure and diversion to nearest suitable airport. After repairs are completed and aircraft is test flown; reporter becomes preoccupied on return flight with engine instruments and enters restricted airspace.
P180 Captain reports baggage door warning passing FL255 in climb. Left engine is shut down in accordance with procedures and flight continues to destination.

A Maintenance Controller reports he authorized a repair to a B757-200 refueling panel lighting wiring by a Fixed Base Operator (FBO); and also signed-off the repair. A downline FAA Inspector noted the repair was not authorized.
ABI controller described possible MOA airspace infraction when intrafactility handoff coordination was less than complete.
B737 Captain reports near collision with tug pulling baggage carts as driver cuts directly in front of aircraft necessitating abrupt braking.
B737 Captain reports complete brake failure during landing roll. Aircraft is brought to stop using reverse thrust alone and is towed to gate.
show: 2009-03 · Ground: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Landing

text: A320 Captain reports being cut off by an airport emergency vehicle at ORD with no lights flashing.

A319 flight crew operating at FL300 with PACK 2 deferred receives ECAM AIRPACK 1+2 FAULT. Crew receives clearance for descent and complies with ECAM procedures which eventually restore PACK 1 operation. Cabin remains below 10000 FT but crew elects to divert for over weight landing.

SR20 pilot reports left brake fails to release after application during landing roll; causing aircraft to depart the runway. Brake releases and aircraft is brought to stop on taxiway. This aircraft has a history of brake problems although maintenance can find nothing wrong and returns aircraft to service.
A BE400 flight crew deviated from the departure procedure track and speed because of a rudder trim failure.

PA32 pilot reports needing external power to start due to weak battery. When the gear handle is raised after takeoff total electrical failure occurs. First landing attempt prompts red light from Tower. While troubleshooting away from the airport electrical power slowly returns to normal.

A C402 pilot noticed a cabin door open warning inflight; followed by the upper half of the door opening. He expressed a lack of confidence in the door warning system since the door light was out before departure.
EMB145 First Officer reports Captain as flying pilot descending early during ILS approach and getting well below glide slope until questioned.
An MD10 flight crew declared an emergency for weather avoidance.
MD80 flight crew experiences a thud at FL240 and continues to destination when no problems can be detected. Post flight reveals a large dent and fan damage to the left engine caused by blue ice.
A B1900 flight crew got a GPWS warning on approach and maneuvered to silence the alarm.
ZJX controller experienced operational error at FL260 when position relief briefing apparently failed to include critical routing information resulting in the loss of separation.
A CRJ900 flight crew experienced a STEERING INOP caution message. They coordinated with dispatch and diverted to a suitable airport.
An A320 Captain reports his right seat belt became loose at the attach point to the seat just before takeoff. Pilot's seat was changed on the previous overnight maintenance service.
A B737-300 flight crew experienced APU failure on takeoff with one generator inoperative. They coordinated with dispatch; ran the procedure; and returned to land at their departure airport.
Altitude deviation occurred on the TEB 5 SID from TEB when a C560XL First Officer accepted a clearance intended for another aircraft.

text: P180 flight crew failed to comply with altitude restrictions on the TEB 5 SID from TEB.
show: 2009-03 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Takeoff

text: A B737-300 flight crew experienced loss of First Officer's flight instruments and other components due to an electrical bus failure. They coordinated with dispatch and diverted to a suitable airport.

B737-300 suffered momentary loss of AC power when the APU was turned off after takeoff. Flight crew quickly realized they had failed to bring the engine generators online prior to takeoff; selecting them on restored AC power.
DHC-8 flight crew rejects takeoff after master caution for #2 AC GEN. After maintenance crew attempts second takeoff with same results; aircraft had a history of generator faults.
Air carrier flight into SNA; held high for VFR traffic executed go around because of unstabilized approach; event may have triggered noise meter.
Embraer 190 Captain experienced repeated failures of autopilot to track the localizer when on a long final.
An ERJ-190 flight crew experienced 'SLAT FAIL' EICAS shortly after takeoff. Maintenance had worked on the slats prior to departure.
A320 experienced multiple bird strikes on landing rollout at IAD.
Cessna 210 suffers engine failure due to fuel starvation when fuel gauge indicated half full although actually empty. A tank change and activation of the electronic fuel pump restarted the engine.
IFR SMT inbound to HOU with I90 experienced conflict at 3000 with unreported traffic; reporter questioned ATC's altitude assignment below Class B.
A PC12 flight crew had a close encounter with a medical helicopter when the Captain taxied onto the runway without calling on CTAF first.

B757 Cabin Attendant attended to a smoke detector alerting in the mid-lavatory. After an assessment; she determined it was attributed to an overheating water heater; advised the Captain and an uneventful landing ensued.
show: 2009-02 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Cruise
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: A Falcon 900EX First Officer reported climbing through charter altitude on the TEB 5 departure.
IFR PA28 departure from HOU received GPWS warning; initially assigned 3000 FT on IDU3 SID and then issued 220 vector; reporter alleging ATC's heading and altitude caused GPWS activation.
CRJ suffered multiple bird strikes on takeoff roll at STL.
The pilot of an experimental Epic LT experienced a complete electrical failure during climb; resulting in a rough running engine. He declared an emergency and returned to his departure airport.
The pilot's failure to declare an emergency following partial engine ignition failure contributed to subsequent track deviations while operating on an IFR flight plan in IMC.
show: 2009-03 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Cruise

text: An Eclipse 500 Captain experienced an unsafe landing gear warning after takeoff. The flight crew ran the procedure and elected to divert to a suitable airport with emergency equipment standing by.
B737NG First Officer relates unexpected encounter with windshear and/or microburst on approach to HOU.

A C310 pilot experienced a nose gear unsafe warning and elected to return to his departure airport for the partial gear landing. Checklist procedures were followed with minimal damage to the aircraft.

During a preflight check on a B737; a First Officer noticed one of the Aileron Power Control Units hydraulic lines was rubbing on a bracket that supports the pivot points of both 'A' and 'B' systems in the left main gear forward wheel well.

A B747-400 Captain reports his concerns about Mechanics and Maintenance Supervisors attempting to coerce flight crews to ignore serious defects; is ongoing and continuous and becoming more commonplace.
An air carrier Flight Attendant reported becoming aware of the presence of a Federal Air Marshal four hours into a transcontinental flight. The flight crew was also unaware of the Marshal's presence.

A B737-800 Captain and First Officer report on contributing factors associated with the Captain continuing to use his Head-up Display (HUD); on approach; even after the Control Tower informed them the airport localizer signal had failed.
show: 2009-03 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Initial Approach

text: An EMB-145's #1 FMS failed followed by CDU BUS FAIL alert displayed in the #1 FMS screen. On the flight's IMC approach an EGPWS 'TERRAIN' warning activated based on the #1 FMS's erroneous position. No procedures were available to deactivate the faulty FMS and to permit valid data for system's operation.
Airbus First Officer removed himself from a trip for fatigue.
CRJ First Officer believes Captain acted unprofessionally when performing passenger landing briefings below 10;000 FT MSL and in the initial approach phase of flight.
Cleared via the CATHEDRAL NINE SID; the flight crew of an A319 failed to fly the teardrop route from PSP to EMRUD and back to PSP prior to joining V370 to TNP.
show: 2009-04 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Initial Climb

text: An Inspector reports about his involvement with the replacement of two cabin door slides on an A319; that were later found with safety pins not removed. Slides at doors 1-Left and 1-Right were inoperative.
A DA-900 experienced an engine failure on departure climb. The flight crew secured the engine; declared an emergency; and diverted to a nearby airport.
PCT Controller described airspace entry event; claiming the FAA established the subject restricted airspace via memo; did not issue any NOTAMs; or inform the user via any other methods.

C172 pilot reports two consecutive precautionary landings while performing test and break-in of rebuilt engine. Carburetor malfunction causes the first and fuel starvation causes the second when fuel that is lost and wasted during the carburetor malfunction is not considered.

CL600 Captain reports track deviation departing LAS Runway 19R on SHEAD5 RNAV. When Captain calls for NAV selection; pilot not flying inadvertently selects HDG causing right turn. Wake turbulence from aircraft departing Runway 25R is encountered at this time; delaying recognition of the inappropriate turn.

A Mechanic working an inbound B757-200 with a cabin door 2R pressure leak; reports the MM 51-11-00-06 procedure to check for leaks; is impossible to comply with. Suggests revising the MM to allow pressurizing the cabin as a suitable alternative.

A light aircraft pilot landing on Runway 03 at TUS was instructed to turn right on Taxiway A2; then was informed a runway incursion had occurred. The commercial airport diagram depicts Taxiway A2; but the government chart does not.

Cleared via the CATHEDRAL NINE SID; the flight crew of a B737NG failed to fly the teardrop route from PSP to EMRUD and back to PSP. Believed crossing at or above the prescribed MCA at PSP obviated the need to do so.
show: 2009-03 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Climb

text: A320 Captain reports nose wheel steering failure while attempting to exit runway after landing. A violent swerve ensues before bringing the aircraft to a stop on the runway. The steering is reset using QRH procedures and the crew continues to the gate.
show: 2009-03 · Ground: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Landing

text: B737 flight crew reports NMAC with flight of three F16's in overhead entry after instructions by Tower to expedite takeoff.

SF340 flight crew reports oil pressure loss on left engine passing 10;000 FT during climb. Engine is shut down and flight returns to departure airport. Outboard tire fails during landing requiring tow to gate.
A transport aircraft experienced a GPWS terrain alert on a night visual approach to OAK Runway 29. The flight crew followed procedures and climbed to end the alert.
After suffering a failure of the right engine; a B767-300 flight crew diverted to the nearest suitable airport for an uneventful landing.
An M20 pilot took off and almost immediately sank back toward the runway for unknown reasons; and was unable to get the landing gear back down before landing.
show: 2008-12 · Ground: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Takeoff

text: A non Pegasus (non GPS) equipped B757 experienced a map shift and track deviation after takeoff even though all applicable preflight procedures were followed intended to ensure FMS performance accuracy.
show: 2009-03 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Initial Climb

text: MD80 First Officer missets altimeter by 1000 FT and Captain does not catch error until aircraft descends below assigned altitude entering holding. Aircraft is quickly brought back to assigned altitude as TCAS traffic alert sounds. Altimeter set at 30.16 instead of 29.16.
A B757-200 flight crew experienced high left engine vibration. They followed procedures and continued to their destination.
An MD11 flight crew noted that #2 throttle could not be retarded below 80% N1. They continued to destination; shut down #2 engine on the descent; and landed normally.
C172 pilot is unable to command his auto pilot to descend too step down fix altitude nor to minimums during practice GPS-B approach to HWD. Reporter passes over airport at 2000 FT.
show: 2009-04 · Procedural: Published Material / Policy · Initial Approach

text: B737 First Officer believed the Captain was derelict in not making a go-around when advised by him that the departing aircraft would not be clear in time.
BE400 on TEB5 SID overshot the initial 1500 FT altitude restriction and experienced a course deviation.
TPA TRACON Controller described proximity event at 10;000 FT; relying on automation assist tool to determine separation; resulting in minimum spacing event.
Bellanca Super Viking suffers partial power loss on takeoff and climb out; possibly the result of water contamination.

Flight Attendant reports the Captain of their transatlantic B767 flight agreed to depart despite a near complete loss of communication capability between the fight deck; the passengers and the cabin attendants.
On climb out the flight crew of a DC10-30 experienced the loss of oil quantity from one engine. After engine was secured the flight continued to a more suitable airport for landing.
B737 Captain failed to comply with NOTAM'd changes to the SHFTY ONE RNAV STAR to RSW.

C207 pilot experienced low oil pressure and oil on windscreen and returns to departure airport. Reporter uses 'urgent' in initial advisory on CTAF and one aircraft; in direct conflict; does not give way. This results in the reporter making delaying turns to increase spacing prior to landing.
Dispatched with an inoperative pack; an MD80 suffered loss of pressurization when the other pack packed it in.
A P180 pilot reported sustaining a lightning strike that shattered the right forward cockpit window. Pressure held; pilot declared an emergency and diverted to nearest suitable airport.

Flight Attendant reports their Saab 340 returned to the departure airport when the left engine was shut down. Felt that less than comprehensive predeparture maintenance action on the engine predicted the event.
Loss of separation in the pattern occurred when the pilot of a small low wing aircraft misidentified traffic he was to follow.

A B777 departed MUC (EDDM) on the GIVMI 3Q. After autopilot engagement the aircraft made a left turn off track then a right turn back on the track. The controller commented that other aircraft had made the same deviation also.
show: 2009-04 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Initial Climb

text: Q400 Flight Crew shut down the left engine and diverted to the nearest suitable airport due to excessive oil pressure indications.
Air carrier inbound to PHX experienced TCAS RA at 5000 during vectors for visual approach to Runway 26.
B757-200 landed with flaps twenty following receipt of a flap asymmetry warning while in cruise.
CRJ200 returned to departure airport following a failure of the flap extend/retract mechanism.
B757-200 returned to departure airport following loss of oil pressure and quantity in the left engine.
TBM8; IFR inbound to APA; began descent and altered pattern before appropriate approach clearance was issued.

Rain water accumulated in a B727 E&E compartment and caused a #2 generator control over/under voltage trip. The crew disconnected the generator. After landing; the voltage regulator was removed; dried out and reinstalled with no further problems.

An air carrier aircraft's radios developed static that interfered with ATC instructions while holding near thunderstorms. The clearance understood by the crew was to LEONA intersection. ATC actually meant LOA VOR (LEONA) which the crew heard phonetically.

A Maintenance Inspector reports he and a Mechanic had signed off for a slide change at cabin door 1-right; on a B737-900; but failed to recognize the slide girt bar was too short and could not be secured in the girt bar floor fittings. A Flight Attendant noticed the discrepancy.

Despite an advisory from the reporter that appropriate NOTAMs were not being provided to flight crews; air carrier Dispatchers continued to dispatch flights without required NOTAMS and failed to advise such flights.
A Captain reports about odor and smoke coming from the First Officer's windshield; that quickly became severe on their DeHavilland DHC-8-400; requiring an emergency return to departure airport.
show: 2009-03 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Climb
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: Unable to communicate with ATC; Mooney M20 pilot descended without clearance to escape icing conditions.
Cessna 750 suffered inappropriate altitude deviations when capturing the glide slope at TEB.
show: 2009-04 · Inflight: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Initial Approach

text: B777 returned to departure airport due to a loud squeal from the Captain's side window. Prior write up had been addressed by maintenance.
B757 Captain reports improper maintenance relative to a chronic failure of the left generator.
B717 returned to departure airport when the right engine failed for unknown reasons during climbout.

Air carrier dispatcher was advised by a flight of a NOTAM'd preferred route through Iraqi airspace which should have been utilized. Company flight operations computer system had failed to flag the NOTAM for appropriate compliance. Reporter cites an unreliable company computer system for the failure to comply.
show: 2009-04 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Cruise

text: VFR C310 departing from PVU entered SLC Class without ATC clearance; reporter citing aircraft performance; airspace limitations; terrain and preflight planning failures and causal factors.
Beechcraft King Air diverted to a suitable airport and landed safely after suffering a catastrophic engine failure.

Failure to properly secure a throttle linkage cotter pin during the manufacture of a Kitfox homebuilt resulted in the loss of throttle control and ultimately a dead stick landing during the initial test flight.
Amphibious homebuilt pilot experienced a close encounter with a speed boat.
Dispatched with an inoperative generator; B757-200 diverted to the nearest suitable airport when the required APU failed in cruise.

After CRJ700 main cabin door retraction system fails and is MEL'ed; Flight Attendant is not briefed by Captain on procedures to follow when opening and closing the door. Door repeatedly falls open causing damage.

A CRJ200 flight crew received an IAS flag and the caution message EFIS COMP MON. They decided to reject the takeoff; but after a second attempt with the same result; water was found in the pitot static system.

B757 Captain notes that the glideslope to Runway 23 at BUF is unusable beyond 5 degrees right of the LOC and may be dangerous when flying a coupled approach. Suggests that stronger language and procedure modification may be in order for this runway in the tailored briefing pages.
show: 2009-04 · Procedural: Published Material / Policy · Initial Approach

text: B737 Captain rejects takeoff for door warning light at 80 KTS. After reclosing the door and waiting for brake cooling flight departs uneventfully.
A B737-700 flight crew experienced momentary loss of control in severe turbulence.
show: 2009-04 · Inflight: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Initial Approach

text: After reaching cruise altitude; an ERJ-170 Captain was asked what were the 'knobs' sticking out of the cabin Passenger Convenience Units (PCU)'s. Upon landing; maintenance informed crew; the 'knobs' were locks; preventing oxygen masks from dropping.

Lear 55 First Officer acting as PIC fails to comply with taxi instructions at TEB; raising the controller's ire. On departure 1500 FT is exceeded on the TEB5 prior to 4.5 DME; while contemplating the botched taxi instructions.
After rotation; BE99 pilot notices both sides of the aft left clamshell are open. Reporter returns for landing where clamshell departs aircraft into the propeller when reverse is selected.
B767-300 Captain reports being dispatched to OBBI which is NOTAM'd closed at the ETA. Error is discovered enroute by dispatcher and aircraft is slowed to arrive after OBBI opening.
A B757 flight crew experienced high left engine vibration. They followed QRH procedure; reduced thrust until vibration was out of caution range; and landed with reduced flap setting.

B757 Captain recounts the exciting events of two missed approaches to a non-radar South American airport; with equipment malfunctions and microburst encounters. Crew declared an emergency and diverted to their alternate; landing with low fuel lights on.
C172 pilot reports being unaware of NOTAM concerning military activity along a line between ACO and YNG 6000 feet and below. Reporter is queried by ATC then given a vector around C-130 traffic.

B767-300 First Officer reports difficulties encountered during a visual approach attempting to placate the Captain; who has strong beliefs about the way the aircraft should be flown that are different from his own.
ZDC controller described loss of separation event at 15;000 during holding procedures when air carrier descended below assigned altitude and conflicted with holding aircraft below.
show: 2009-04 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Initial Approach

text: B737 flight crew departs SLC with a PACK on MEL after rumbling noise is heard during taxi and ice in PACK is suspected as the cause. Cabin altitude begins to rise with single PACK operation at FL250 and crew elects to use the deferred PACK rather than descend. This works and flight continues to destination.
B737 Captain reported auto pressurization failure at FL330. Emergency was declared and descent initiated. Manual control of the system was gained at 18;000 FT and flight continued to destination.
BE1900 flight crew report directional control and braking problems during landing roll. Crew is unable to stop aircraft prior to nose gear departing runway. No damage or injuries occurred.
Civilian helo on departure from a helicopter site and a military helo have a NMAC at night.

C402 reports door warning light prior to start after all doors are closed. After checking all doors and hatches and knowing of maintenance history; door warning light is MEL'ed. During takeoff hatch comes open and takeoff is rejected.
Air carrier on visual approach to IWA experienced TCAS RA with light traffic near FFZ; claiming Class B needs revision to avoid similar events.

CRJ700 Captain discovers CG to be out of limits during manual weight and balance calculation. Problem is traced to incorrect balance arm calculated after most recent aircraft reweigh. Maintenance and dispatch are unaware of the new number.
Learjet 55 flight crew on the TEB 5 departure; exceeds the initial 1500 foot restriction by 300 FT.
C172 inbound to MGJ on ILS 3 approach completed circling maneuver which resulted in loss of separation.
Lear 60 Captain reports altitude deviation during the Dalton departure from Runway 19 at TEB; citing turbulence and lack of support from his copilot as the primary reasons for the deviation.
MIA Local Controller described near taxiway landing event when C172; cleared to land on runway 8L; made an approach to taxiway K; ATC issued go-around.
FAI Local Controller described flawed ZAN sequencing/spacing event with two arrival aircraft; alleging ZAN Controller failed to adequately complete the visual approach process.
Runway excursion causing no damage followed a loss of control on landing by Piper J3 student and instructor pilots.
A PA28 pilot on a long cross country but without a flight plan lost flight following contact with ATC over the mountains. Lack of communication triggered preparation for a search.

Large commercial aircraft Captain refuses an aircraft for an oceanic flight with deferred automatic speed brake deployment. Company proceeded to shop for another Captain that would take the flight and charged the refusing Captain with an operational disruption.
Stinson 108 pilot encountered rough running engine and diverted to a nearby airport. Cause determined to be carburetor icing.
Learjet cleared into position for takeoff on Runway 34 at HPN; was issued an abort; traffic on final sent around; ATC indicated vehicle traffic on departure end of runway caused event.
A B737-300 flight crew found themselves short of fuel when their destination instituted holding; so they declared an emergency to minimize the delay.
A320 Captain reports bird strike at 1500 FT on departure. Emergency is declared and flight returns to departure airport for inspection.
ZID Controller experienced loss of separation at FL340 when climbing aircraft slowed to unexpected rate creating the conflict; weather chop listed as possible factor.
B737 lost thrust on right engine shortly after takeoff. Power returned during initial climb and flight crew diverted to a nearby airport.
B747-400 dumps fuel and returns to departure airport when landing gear fails to retract after takeoff.

B767-300 Captain reports attempting to exit Runway 13L at JFK on Taxiway ZA; to discover it closed and coned off. Reporter had no prior notification via NOTAMs or ATIS. Dispatchers report explains the possible reason this occurred.

B737 flight crew reports low N1 during takeoff and elects to continue. Once airborne; and after discussing issue with maintenance; the decision is made to return. The engine runs normally throughout the return and landing.
B767 flight crew descending into MROC with an aggressive descent rate received a GPWS terrain alert.

Helicopter allegedly entered DFW Class B without a clearance after being denied a SVFR transition clearance through the subject Class B; reporter claiming DFW TRACON Controllers were less than helpful or knowledgeable regarding SVFR.
A300 flight crew on departure from CLE experienced a bird strike.
ZOB Controller described operational deviation when aircraft entered adjacent airspace without coordination and/or handoff; citing automation entry error as the causal factor.

A Captain reports that he and the First Officer were charged with a delay for refusing to accept two deferrals for the same hot air valve on an A320; with the temperature uncontrollable. Captain questions how can a system legally be deferred; when the back up system is not working properly?

A320 flight crew reports flap fault during approach and subsequent go around. Fault does not generate a warning chime or light and flaps appear to move to selected position. Crew elects to land with flaps 1 and no ECAM message.
Dispatcher reports that not all NOTAMs for a given airport are being printed by the companies flight planning computer.

An air carrier aircraft's FMC did not accept a flight plan along UM869 because UM869 terminated in the FMC database at GOREV intersection west bound. The navigation chart and aircraft database were in error because a change extending that airway was not received.

B757-200 flight crew in cruise experienced a loud bang followed by a rise in number 2 engine EGT and smoke smell reported in the cabin. They shutdown the engine; elected to divert for weather and had a subsequent APU failure on approach.

text: ZMA Controller providing OJT experienced operational error at FL370/360 when issued traffic altitude information was acknowledged as descent clearance; reporter/developmental both failed to note incorrect pilot response.
CRJ with a single pack deferred departed only to have a pressurization problem climbing through 16;000 FT.
AVL Controller described near loss of separation involving two overflight aircraft; descending both during an overtake situation; Controller corrective action saved separation.
A Q400 got a GPWS TERRAIN warning on the RNAV 34L approach to RNO. The flight crew executed a go-around per policy and accepted a vector to a south landing.
B757 flight crew experiences an FMS map shift during the KENNEDY1 departure from JFK. ATC issued vectors to return flight to desired track.

text: BE90 First Officer reports engine failure at during climbout. Engine is shut down; propeller feathered; and flight diverts to suitable airport.

ZAB Controller described IFR vectoring event involving a clearance issued below legal altitude limitations.

text: Regional jet flight crew in cruise received a master warning BAGG SMOKE on EICAS; after running the checklist; the EICAS message extinguished however the illuminated button remained. Flight crew elected to declare an emergency and divert to an enroute airport.

B757 flight crew is informed in cruise that a smoke alarm has activated in a lavatory. Smoke is seen and smelled; and the lavatory wall is hot to the touch. Attempts at control using circuit breakers are unsuccessful and flight diverts to nearest suitable airport.

text: EMB-140 flight crew enroute received a master caution SPOILER FAIL message on the EICAS; ran the procedure; declared an emergency and made an uneventful landing at destination.
C172 pilot on approach to ERV experienced an NMAC with same direction traffic who thought they had this pilot in sight; but turned out to be a different target.
IFR aircraft with PCT at 4000 landing IAD failed to adhere to speed requirements below Class B airspace; citing ATC failed to insure aircraft remained within the confines of protected airspace.
CH601; Zenith Zodiac; Instructor pilot experienced a prop strike when the student locked up on the brakes prior to touchdown.
show: 2009-04 · Ground: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Landing

text: Air carrier with ZDC climbing to FL360 experienced TCAS RA with opposite direction traffic; ATC issued expedited climb; TCAS commanded and crew initiated descent.
A Falcon 2000 flight crew flew through an altitude restriction on the TEB departure; in part because of autopilot problems.
SF340 Captain experiences Np gauge malfunction then failure with torque fluctuations and high ITT. Crew elects to divert to nearest suitable airport.

A320 Captain reports Green hydraulic System high temperature during climb out. ECAM procedures are complied with and crew elects to return to departure airport. Green hydraulic pump is turned on just prior to landing.

B737NG Captain experiences LEFT ELECT HYD Pump OVHT during climb out. QRH procedures are complied with and crew elects to return to departure airport when communications cannot be established with maintenance.
B767 Relief Pilot is informed during rest break; that fuel gauge problems are necessitating a return. Some fuel is dumped but aircraft still lands over weight.
Lear 55 flight crew reports departing right edge of runway after landing due to asymmetrical thrust reverser deployment and minimal braking on one wheel on the left side.

B757 Captain reports R engine compressor stall at FL340. After comparison with good L engine. Engine is shut down. APU fails during descent. Uneventful landing ensues at destination. Maintenance discovers P1 leak on good engine which skewed both EPR and EGT readings in flight.
show: 2009-04 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Cruise
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: PA31 pilot reports jammed elevator during climb out. After further investigation diagnosis turns to run away electric trim. Trim circuit breaker is pulled and remainder of flight is normal.
Instructor and student on IFR cross country training flight in VMC only aircraft are unable to remain clear of clouds despite informing controller of their limitations.
MD80 flight crew experiences EGPWS terrain warning 4 miles north of DEN at 9000 FT; after go-around from Runway 35L. Crew heeds warning and climbs to 10000 FT.

text: Piper J3 Cub pilot practicing crosswind landings has runway excursion during landing roll out. Aircraft is taxied back to the ramp and inspected where no damage is found.
C172 pilot landed in strong crosswind; lost control momentarily; and propeller blades made contact with runway.
show: 2009-04 · Ground: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Landing

text: B757 flight crew reports LE SLAT DISAGREE during approach. Crew accomplishes QRH procedure and lands with full flaps and slats using the ALTN FLAP and SLAT selector switches.

Air carrier flight crew at EAU had a near runway incursion while taxiing out for departure; First Officer recognized the situation in time to avoid the incursion; but cites the lack of signage as a contributing factor.
CRJ700 Captain reports SLATS FAIL message during approach. While accomplishing SLATS FAIL QRH procedure; reporter drifts into Flaps Fail checklist which results in 0 flap landing unnecessarily.
show: 2009-04 · Procedural: Published Material / Policy · Initial Approach

text: A leaking fueling cap was discovered and corrected prior to boarding of an A320. 831858	DGN
A320 flight crew received HYD GRN RES LO LVL ECAM message and responded accordingly.

B737 Captain reports TCAS RA during ILS approach to Runway 35L with aircraft on approach to 35R at DEN. RA is complied with and eventual go-around results. Controller questions need for RA compliance and go-around.
A319 encounters a bus attempting to cross a taxiway ahead of them. A stalemate occurred requiring law enforcement to intervene.

A319 flight crew reports wake turbulence encounter at 3500 FT on departure from preceding B767. Encounter causes mild jostling and a momentary compressor stall. Crew elects to return to departure airport for over weight landing.
While still in domestic airspace; a B747-400 dumped fuel and diverted due to a fuel leak.
Flight crew; including FFDO; was not informed of presence of two FAMs on a domestic B767 flight.
E145 flight crew shut down an engine and diverted due to low oil pressure and quantity.
TCAS RA saves the day for an MD88 flight crew and an unrepentant light twin pilot who had just canceled IFR.
Jetranger pilot is unable to contact LGA Tower while performing a tour of New York City. Violation of New York Class B results.
FAI Controller described likely pilot deviation with regard to initial heading assignment off EIL. Reporter alleged management not processing military pilot and controller errors.
show: 2009-04 · Deviation - Track / Heading All Types · Takeoff

text: A Lead Mechanic; Maintenance Inspector and Maintenance Supervisor report on their involvement with an ATR-72-200 aircraft that was found with incorrectly installed right aileron attach bolts; prior to flight.
EMB-140 flight crew received LG LEVER DISAGREE EICAS warning on departure. They run the procedures; declare an emergency and returned to an uneventful landing.
Newly required aisle lights were shorted out by an overflowed toilet in a Citation CJ3; the single pilot; after recognizing smoke; declared an emergency and diverted.
show: 2009-04 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Cruise
